bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第267卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 267
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 267

sentences.zh: 【後梁紀二】起著雍執徐八月，盡重光協洽二月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: 【Later Liang Annals II】 Beginning in the eighth month of the year gengxu, ending in the second month of the year gengyin; in all, a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Later Liang Annals II】 From the eighth month of 909 through the second month of 912—a span of slightly more than two years.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳越王鏐遣寧國節度使王景仁奉表詣大梁，陳取淮南之策。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, King Qian Liu of Wuyue sent Ningguo military governor Wang Jingren to present a memorial at Daliang, setting forth a plan to seize Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wuyue's King Qian Liu sent his Ningguo military governor Wang Jingren to Daliang with a memorial outlining a strategy for taking Huainan.

sentences.zh: 景仁即茂章也，避梁諱改焉。

translations.literal: Jingren was originally Maozhang; he changed his name to avoid the taboo of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren had formerly been called Maozhang; he had changed his name to avoid a taboo of the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 淮南遣步軍都指揮使周本、南面統軍使呂師造擊吳越，九月，圍蘇州。

translations.literal: Huainan sent infantry commander Zhou Ben and southern army commander Lü Shizao to attack Wuyue; in the ninth month, they besieged Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan dispatched its infantry commander Zhou Ben and southern army commander Lü Shizao against Wuyue; in the ninth month they laid siege to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳越將張仁保攻常州之東洲，拔之。

translations.literal: The Wuyue general Zhang Renbao attacked Dongzhou in Changzhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyue general Zhang Renbao attacked Dongzhou in Changzhou and took it.

sentences.zh: 淮南兵死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Huainan soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 淮南以池州團練使陳璋為水陸行營都招討使，帥柴再用等諸將救東洲，大破仁保於魚蕩，復取東洲。

translations.literal: Huainan appointed Chizhou regimental training commissioner Chen Zhang as overall commander of the land-and-water campaign, leading generals including Chai Zaiyong to relieve Dongzhou; they routed Renbao at Yudang and recovered Dongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan made Chizhou regimental commissioner Chen Zhang overall commander of the joint land-and-water force and sent him with Chai Zaiyong and other generals to relieve Dongzhou; at Yudang they crushed Zhang Renbao and retook Dongzhou.

sentences.zh: 柴再用方戰舟壞，長槊浮之，僅而得濟。

translations.literal: Chai Zaiyong was in the midst of battle when his boat was wrecked; he floated on a long spear and barely got across.
translations.idiomatic: During the fighting Chai Zaiyong's boat was smashed; he clung to a long spear to stay afloat and barely made it ashore.

sentences.zh: 家人為之飯僧千人，再用悉取其食以犒部兵，曰：「士卒濟我，僧何力焉！

translations.literal: His family had prepared food for a thousand monks on his behalf; Zaiyong took all of it to reward his troops, saying, "The soldiers saved me—what power had the monks!
translations.idiomatic: His family had arranged a feast for a thousand monks in his honor; Zaiyong took all the food to reward his troops, saying, "It was the soldiers who saved me—what did the monks do for me!

sentences.zh: 丙子，蜀立皇后周氏。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Shu installed Lady Zhou as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Shu invested Lady Zhou as empress.

sentences.zh: 后，許州人也。

translations.literal: The empress was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉周德威、李嗣昭將兵三萬出陰地關，攻晉州，刺史徐懷玉拒守。

translations.literal: Jin's Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao led thirty thousand troops out through Yindi Pass to attack Jinzhou; prefect Xu Huaiyu held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao marched thirty thousand men through Yindi Pass against Jinzhou, where prefect Xu Huaiyu shut himself in to resist.

sentences.zh: 帝自將救之，丁丑，發大梁，乙酉，至陝州。

translations.literal: The emperor personally led troops to relieve it; on the day dingchou he set out from Daliang, and on the day yiyou he reached Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led a relief force in person; on dingchou he left Daliang and on yiyou reached Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，岐王所署延州節度使胡敬璋寇上平關，劉知俊擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Yanzhou military governor Hu Jingzhang, appointed by the Prince of Qi, raided Shangping Pass; Liu Zhijun defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Yanzhou military governor Hu Jingzhang, whom the Prince of Qi had commissioned, raided Shangping Pass; Liu Zhijun routed him.

sentences.zh: 周德威等聞帝將至，乙未，退保隰州。

translations.literal: When Zhou Dewei and the others heard that the emperor was coming, on the day yiwei they withdrew and held Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the emperor was on his way, Zhou Dewei and his colleagues fell back to Xi Prefecture on yiwei.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高季昌遣兵屯漢口，絕楚朝貢之路。

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Gao Jichang sent troops to encamp at Hankou and cut off the route by which Chu paid tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan military governor Gao Jichang posted troops at Hankou, severing the route by which Chu sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷遣其將許德勳將水軍擊之，至沙頭，季昌懼而請和。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu sent his general Xu Dexun with a naval force to attack him; when they reached Shatou, Jichang became afraid and sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: King Ma Yin of Chu sent his general Xu Dexun with a fleet against him; when the Chu ships reached Shatou, Jichang grew alarmed and sought peace.

sentences.zh: 殷又遣步軍都指揮使呂師周將兵擊嶺南，與清海節度使劉隱十餘戰，取昭、賀、梧、蒙、龔、富六州。

translations.literal: Yin also sent infantry commander Lü Shizhou with troops to strike Lingnan; after more than ten battles with Qinghai military governor Liu Yin, he took the six prefectures of Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin also sent infantry commander Lü Shizhou into Lingnan; after more than ten engagements with Qinghai military governor Liu Yin he seized the six prefectures of Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 殷土宇既廣，乃養士息民，湖南遂安。

translations.literal: Yin's territory having grown broad, he then nurtured scholars and let the people rest; Hunan was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With his domain greatly enlarged, Yin began to patronize scholars and give the people respite, and Hunan grew secure.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，蜀主立後宮張氏為貴妃，徐氏為賢妃，其妹為德妃。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the ruler of Shu installed Zhang of the inner palace as noble consort, the Xu clan as wise consort, and her younger sister as virtuous consort.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Shu ruler elevated Zhang of the inner palace to noble consort, a lady of the Xu clan to wise consort, and her younger sister to virtuous consort.

sentences.zh: 張氏，郪人，宗懿之母也。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan were people of Qi; she was the mother of Zongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was from Qi and was the mother of Zongyi.

sentences.zh: 二徐，耕之女也。

translations.literal: The two Xu were daughters of Geng.
translations.idiomatic: The two Xu sisters were daughters of Xu Geng.

sentences.zh: 華原賊帥溫韜聚眾嵯峨山，暴掠雍州諸縣，唐帝諸陵發之殆遍。

translations.literal: The Huayuan bandit chief Wen Tao gathered a host on Cuo'e Mountain, ravaging the counties of Yong Prefecture; he had opened nearly all the tombs of the Tang emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayuan bandit leader Wen Tao rallied men on Cuo'e Mountain and plundered the counties of Yong Prefecture; he had looted almost every Tang imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，蜀主講武於星宿山，步騎三十萬。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the ruler of Shu reviewed troops on Xingxiu Mountain—three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Shu ruler held a grand military review on Xingxiu Mountain with three hundred thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，帝還大梁。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, the emperor returned to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor returned to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以劉隱為清海、靜海節度使，以膳部郎中趙光裔、右補闕李殷衡充官告使，隱皆留之。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Liu Yin was made military governor of Qinghai and Jinghai; Ministry of Rites bureau director Zhao Guangyi and right remonstrance official Li Yinheng were sent as credential-bearers, and Yin kept them all.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Liu Yin was appointed military governor of Qinghai and Jinghai; Zhao Guangyi of the Ministry of Rites and right remonstrance official Li Yinheng were dispatched as credential envoys, and Yin detained them all.

sentences.zh: 光裔，光逢之弟；

translations.literal: Guangyi was the younger brother of Guangfeng;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyi was a younger brother of Zhao Guangfeng;

sentences.zh: 殷衡，德裕之孫也。

translations.literal: Yinheng was a grandson of Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yinheng was a grandson of Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 依政進士梁震，唐末登第，至是歸蜀。

translations.literal: Yizheng metropolitan graduate Liang Zhen had passed the examinations at the end of Tang; at this time he returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen of Yizheng, a metropolitan graduate who had passed the examinations late in Tang, now returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 過江陵，高季昌愛其才識，留之，欲奏為判官。

translations.literal: Passing through Jiangling, Gao Jichang admired his talent and kept him, wishing to memorialize the court to appoint him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jiangling, Gao Jichang was taken with his ability and detained him, intending to recommend him as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 震恥之，欲去，恐及禍，乃曰：「震素不慕榮宦，明公不以震為愚，必欲使之參謀議，但以白衣侍樽俎可也，何必在幕府！

translations.literal: Zhen was ashamed of this and wished to leave, but feared disaster; he therefore said, "Zhen has never coveted rank and office. If my lord does not think Zhen a fool and must have him take part in counsel, let him attend your table in plain dress—that is enough; why must he be in the headquarters!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was ashamed and wanted to leave, yet feared reprisal; he said, "I have never coveted rank. If you do not think me a fool and truly want my counsel, let me attend your table as a private guest—that is enough; why must I sit in your headquarters!

sentences.zh: 」季昌許之。

translations.literal: " Jichang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jichang consented.

sentences.zh: 震終身止稱前進士，不受高氏辟署。

translations.literal: Zhen for his whole life called himself only a former metropolitan graduate and would not accept appointment from the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of his life Zhen styled himself only a former metropolitan graduate and never accepted formal appointment from the Gao family.

sentences.zh: 季昌甚重之，以為謀主，呼曰先輩。

translations.literal: Jichang greatly valued him, made him his chief strategist, and addressed him as Senior.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang held him in high esteem, treated him as chief strategist, and addressed him as Senior.

sentences.zh: 帝從吳越王鏐之請，以亳州團練使寇彥卿為東南面行營都指揮使，擊淮南。

translations.literal: The emperor, acceding to King Qian Liu of Wuyue's request, appointed Bozhou regimental training commissioner Kou Yanqing as overall commander of the southeastern campaign and sent him against Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At King Qian Liu of Wuyue's request, the emperor made Bozhou regimental commissioner Kou Yanqing overall commander of the southeastern campaign and sent him against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，彥卿帥眾二千襲霍丘，為土豪朱景所敗；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yanqing led two thousand men in a surprise attack on Huoqiu and was defeated by the local strongman Zhu Jing;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yanqing led two thousand men in a raid on Huoqiu and was beaten by local magnate Zhu Jing;

sentences.zh: 又攻廬、壽二州，皆不勝。

translations.literal: he then attacked the two prefectures of Lu and Shou but was victorious in neither.
translations.idiomatic: he then attacked Lu and Shou prefectures but failed in both.

sentences.zh: 淮南遣滁州刺史史儼拒之，彥卿引歸。

translations.literal: Huainan sent Chuzhou prefect Shi Yan to resist him, and Yanqing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan sent Chuzhou prefect Shi Yan against him, and Yanqing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 定難節度使李思諫卒；

translations.literal: Dingnan military governor Li Sijian died;
translations.idiomatic: Dingnan military governor Li Sijian died;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，其子彝昌自為留後。

translations.literal: on the day jiaxu, his son Yichang made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: on jiaxu his son Yichang installed himself as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 劉守文舉滄德兵攻幽州，劉守光求救於晉，晉王遣兵五千助之。

translations.literal: Liu Shouwen raised the troops of Cang and De to attack Youzhou; Liu Shouguang sought aid from Jin, and the Prince of Jin sent five thousand troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouwen mobilized the armies of Cang and De against Youzhou; Liu Shouguang appealed to Jin, and the Prince of Jin sent five thousand men to his aid.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，守文兵至盧台軍，為守光所敗；

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Shouwen's army reached Lutai Army and was defeated by Shouguang;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Shouwen's army reached Lutai Army and was defeated by Shouguang;

sentences.zh: 又戰玉田，亦敗。

translations.literal: they fought again at Yutian and were again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: they fought again at Yutian and lost once more.

sentences.zh: 守文乃還。

translations.literal: Shouwen then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，中書侍郎、同平章事張策以刑部尚書致仕；

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister Zhang Ce retired as Minister of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister Zhang Ce retired as Minister of Justice;

sentences.zh: 以左僕射楊涉同平章事。

translations.literal: Left vice director of the Department of State Affairs Yang She was made co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yang She was made co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 保塞節度使胡敬璋卒，靜難節度使李繼徽以其將劉萬子代鎮延州。

translations.literal: Baosai military governor Hu Jingzhang died; Jingnan military governor Li Jihui sent his general Liu Wanzi to replace him and hold Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Baosai military governor Hu Jingzhang died; Jingnan military governor Li Jihui sent his general Liu Wanzi to take over Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，弘農王遣軍將萬全感繼書間道詣晉及岐，告以嗣位。

translations.literal: That year, the King of Hongnong sent the army officer Wan Quangan with a letter by a secret route to Jin and to Qi, announcing his succession.
translations.idiomatic: That year the King of Hongnong sent army officer Wan Quangan with a letter by a secret route to Jin and Qi to announce his succession.

sentences.zh: 帝將遷都洛陽。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to move the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to move the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳，遷太廟神主於洛陽。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jisi, the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple were moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jisi the spirit tablets of the imperial ancestral temple were moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, the emperor set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the emperor left Daliang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以博王友文為東都留守。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Prince of Bo Youwen was made eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Prince of Bo Zhu Youwen was made regent of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝至洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the emperor reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the emperor arrived in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，饗太廟。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, he offered sacrifice in the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he offered sacrifice in the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，祀圓丘，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, he sacrificed at the Round Mound and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he sacrificed at the Round Mound and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以用度稍充，初給百官全俸。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, because revenues had grown somewhat sufficient, full salaries were for the first time paid to all officials.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, with revenues somewhat improved, full salaries were paid to officials for the first time.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the month dingyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day dingyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 保塞節度使劉萬子暴虐，失眾心，且謀貳於梁，李繼徽使延州牙將李延實圖之。

translations.literal: Baosai military governor Liu Wanzi was cruel and tyrannical and lost the hearts of his men; moreover he plotted to go over to Liang. Li Jihui sent Yanzhou garrison officer Li Yanshi to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: Baosai military governor Liu Wanzi was brutal and lost the loyalty of his troops; he also plotted to defect to Liang. Li Jihui sent Yanzhou garrison officer Li Yanshi to deal with him.

sentences.zh: 延實因萬子葬胡敬璋，攻而殺之，遂據延州。

translations.literal: Yanshi, taking advantage of Wanzi's burial of Hu Jingzhang, attacked and killed him and then seized Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Wanzi's funeral for Hu Jingzhang, Yanshi struck, killed him, and seized Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 馬軍都指揮使河西高萬興與其弟萬金聞變，以其眾數千人詣劉知俊降。

translations.literal: Cavalry commander Hexi Gao Wanxing and his younger brother Wanjin, hearing of the upheaval, came with several thousand of their troops to Liu Zhijun and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Gao Wanxing of Hexi and his brother Wanjin, hearing of the turmoil, brought several thousand men to Liu Zhijun and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 岐王置翟州於鄜城，其守將亦降。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi had established Zhai Prefecture at Fucheng; its defending general also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi had established Zhai Prefecture at Fucheng; its garrison commander surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，帝發洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiaxu, the emperor set out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiaxu the emperor left Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以山南東道節度使楊師厚兼潞州四面行營招討使。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou was additionally made commander of the four-sided campaign against Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou was also made commander of the encircling campaign against Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝至河中，發步騎會高萬興兵取丹、延。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the emperor reached Hezhong and dispatched infantry and cavalry to join Gao Wanxing's troops in taking Dan and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor reached Hezhong and sent foot and horse to join Gao Wanxing in taking Dan and Yan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以朔方節度使兼中書令韓遜為穎川王。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Shuofang military governor and concurrent Palace Secretariat director Han Xun was made Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Shuofang military governor and concurrent Secretariat director Han Xun was created Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 遜本靈州牙校，唐末據本鎮，前廷因而授以節鉞。

translations.literal: Xun had originally been a garrison officer of Lingzhou; at the end of Tang he seized his own circuit, and the former court thereupon granted him the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had been a garrison officer at Lingzhou; late in Tang he seized his circuit, and the former court had granted him a military commission in recognition.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，丹州刺史崔公實請降。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Danzhou prefect Cui Gongshi requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Danzhou prefect Cui Gongshi offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 徐溫以金陵形勝，戰艦所聚，乃自以淮南行軍副使領升州刺史，留廣陵，以其假子元從指揮使知誥為升州隊遏兼樓船副使，往治之。

translations.literal: Xu Wen, because Jinling was strategically strong and a gathering place for warships, personally took the post of Shengzhou prefect as Huainan deputy campaign commander, remaining at Guangling; he sent his adopted son Yuancong, commander Zhigao, as Shengzhou patrol and deputy riverine commander to go and administer it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jinling was strategically vital and a concentration point for warships, Xu Wen took the Shengzhou prefecture himself as Huainan deputy campaign commander while remaining at Guangling; he sent his adopted son Yuancong, commander Zhigao, as Shengzhou patrol officer and deputy riverine commander to govern it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙申朔，劉知俊移軍攻延州，李延實嬰城自守。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day bingchen, Liu Zhijun moved his army to attack Yanzhou; Li Yanshi shut the city and held out.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day bingchen Liu Zhijun marched against Yanzhou; Li Yanshi barred the gates and defended the city.

sentences.zh: 知俊遣白水鎮使劉儒分兵圍坊州。

translations.literal: Zhijun sent Baishui garrison commissioner Liu Ru with a detachment to besiege Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun sent Baishui garrison commissioner Liu Ru with a detachment to besiege Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以王審知為閩王，劉隱為南平王。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Wang Shenzhi was made Prince of Min and Liu Yin Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Wang Shenzhi was created Prince of Min and Liu Yin Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊克延州，李延實降。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun captured Yanzhou; Li Yanshi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun took Yanzhou and Li Yanshi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 淮南兵圍蘇州，推洞屋攻城，吳越將臨海孫琰置輪於竿首，垂絲亙投錐以揭之，攻者盡露，砲至則張網以拒之，淮南人不能克。

translations.literal: Huainan troops besieged Suzhou, advancing siege sheds to assault the walls; the Wuyue general Linhai Sun Yan placed wheels atop poles, hung silk across them, and cast hooks to lift them—exposing all the attackers; when catapults came, nets were spread to block them, and the Huainan men could not overcome the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan forces besieged Suzhou with rolling siege sheds; Wuyue general Sun Yan of Linhai mounted wheels on pole tops, stretched silk between them, and cast grappling hooks to raise the sheds—exposing every attacker; when stones flew, defenders spread nets to catch them, and Huainan could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐遣牙內指揮使錢鏢、行軍副使杜建徽等將兵救之。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue sent palace guard commander Qian Biao, deputy campaign commander Du Jianhui, and others with troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu sent palace guard commander Qian Biao, deputy campaign commander Du Jianhui, and others with a relief army.

sentences.zh: 蘇州有水通城中，淮南張網綴鈴懸水中，魚鱉過皆知之。

translations.literal: Suzhou had waterways leading into the city; Huainan stretched nets with bells attached and hung them in the water—when fish or turtles passed, they all knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Waterways ran from outside into Suzhou; Huainan strung nets rigged with bells in the channels so that any fish or turtle passing would set them off.

sentences.zh: 吳越游弈都虞候司馬福欲潛行入城，故以竿觸網，敵聞鈴聲舉網，福因得過，凡居水中三日，乃得入城。

translations.literal: The Wuyue patrol commander Sima Fu wished to steal into the city; he deliberately touched the nets with a pole, and when the enemy heard the bells they raised the nets—Fu thereby got through; he stayed in the water altogether three days before he could enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue patrol commander Sima Fu wanted to slip into the city; he deliberately brushed the nets with a pole, and when the enemy heard the bells they hauled the nets up—Fu slipped through; he spent three full days in the water before reaching the city.

sentences.zh: 由是城中號令與援兵相應，敵以為神。

translations.literal: From this the commands within the city and the relief troops answered each other; the enemy thought it supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter orders inside the city coordinated with the relief force, and the enemy took it for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐嘗游府園，見園卒陸仁章樹藝有智而志之，及蘇州被圍，使仁章通信入城，果得報而返。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue had once toured the government garden and, seeing the gardener Lu Renzhang's skill in planting and his intelligence, took note of him; when Suzhou was besieged, he sent Renzhang with messages into the city, and he indeed obtained a reply and returned.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu had once toured the government gardens, noted gardener Lu Renzhang's skill and sharp mind, and remembered him; when Suzhou was besieged he sent Renzhang with messages into the city, and Renzhang brought back a reply as promised.

sentences.zh: 鏐以諸孫畜之，累遷兩府軍糧都監使，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: Liu raised him like a grandson, promoted him repeatedly, and eventually made him overseer of grain for both prefectures; in the end he proved useful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu raised him like a grandson, promoted him steadily, and eventually made him overseer of grain for both prefectures—he proved his worth in the end.

sentences.zh: 仁章，睦州人也。

translations.literal: Renzhang was a native of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhang was from Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，吳越兵內外合擊淮南兵，大破之，擒其將何朗等三十餘人，奪戰艦二百艘。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Wuyue troops inside and outside joined in attacking the Huainan army and routed them utterly, capturing more than thirty of their generals including He Lang and seizing two hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wuyue forces inside and outside the city struck the Huainan army together, crushing them, capturing more than thirty officers including He Lang, and taking two hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 周本夜遁，又追敗之於皇天蕩。

translations.literal: Zhou Ben fled by night; they pursued and defeated him again at Huangtiandang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben fled by night; the pursuers defeated him again at Huangtiandang.

sentences.zh: 鍾泰章將精兵二百為殿，多樹旗幟於菰蔣中，追兵不敢進而還。

translations.literal: Zhong Taizhang led two hundred elite troops as rearguard and planted many banners and flags among the reeds and rushes; the pursuers dared not advance and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Taizhang covered the retreat with two hundred picked troops and planted many banners among the reeds; the pursuers dared not press on and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 岐王所署保大節度使李彥博、坊州刺史李彥昱皆棄城奔鳳翔，鄜州都將嚴弘倚舉城降。

translations.literal: Baoda military governor Li Yanbo and Fangzhou prefect Li Yanyu, both appointed by the Prince of Qi, abandoned their cities and fled to Fengxiang; Fuzhou garrison commander Yan Hongyi surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Baoda military governor Li Yanbo and Fangzhou prefect Li Yanyu, both Qi appointees, abandoned their posts and fled to Fengxiang; Fuzhou garrison commander Yan Hongyi surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 己未，以高萬興為保塞節度使，以絳州刺史牛存節為保大節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Gao Wanxing was made Baosai military governor and Jiangzhou prefect Niu Cunjie was made Baoda military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Gao Wanxing was appointed Baosai military governor and Jiangzhou prefect Niu Cunjie Baoda military governor.

sentences.zh: 淮南初置選舉，以駱知祥掌之。

translations.literal: Huainan for the first time established civil examinations and put Luo Zhixiang in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan established civil examinations for the first time and placed Luo Zhixiang in charge.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁卯，帝命劉知俊乘勝取邠州，知俊難之，辭以闕食，乃召還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingmao, the emperor ordered Liu Zhijun to press his victory and take Bin Prefecture; Zhijun found it difficult and declined on the ground of lack of provisions, and was then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingmao the emperor ordered Liu Zhijun to follow up and take Bin Prefecture; Zhijun demurred, citing lack of supplies, and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 佑國節度使王重師鎮長安數年，帝在河中，怒其貢奉不時，己巳，召重師入朝，以左龍虎統軍劉捍為佑國留後。

translations.literal: Youguo military governor Wang Chongshi had held Chang'an for several years; the emperor was at Hezhong and was angry that his tribute was not timely; on the day jisi he summoned Chongshi to court and made Left Dragon-Tiger commander Liu Han Youguo regent.
translations.idiomatic: Youguo military governor Wang Chongshi had governed Chang'an for years; while the emperor was at Hezhong he grew angry that Chongshi's tribute was late; on jisi he summoned Chongshi to court and made Left Dragon-Tiger commander Liu Han regent of Youguo.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝發河中；

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the emperor set out from Hezhong;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor left Hezhong;

sentences.zh: 己卯，至洛陽。

translations.literal: on the day jimao, he reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: on jimao he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 劉捍至長安，王重師不為禮，捍譖之於帝，雲重師潛與邠、岐通。

translations.literal: When Liu Han reached Chang'an, Wang Chongshi did not treat him with courtesy; Han slandered him to the emperor, saying Chongshi was secretly in communication with Bin and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Han arrived in Chang'an, Wang Chongshi slighted him; Han denounced him to the emperor, claiming Chongshi was secretly in league with Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 甲申，貶重師溪州刺史，尋賜自盡，夷其族。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Chongshi was demoted to prefect of Xi and soon ordered to take his own life; his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Chongshi was demoted to prefect of Xi and soon ordered to kill himself; his entire clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 劉守文頻年攻劉守光不克，力大發兵，以重賂招契丹、吐谷渾之眾，合四萬屯薊州。

translations.literal: Liu Shouwen for years had attacked Liu Shouguang without success; he mustered his strength and raised a great army, and with heavy bribes recruited the hosts of Khitan and Tuyuhun; together forty thousand encamped at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouwen had attacked Liu Shouguang for years without success; he now raised a large force and, with lavish bribes, enlisted Khitan and Tuyuhun troops—forty thousand in all encamped at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 守光逆戰於雞蘇，為守文所敗。

translations.literal: Shouguang met him in battle at Jisu and was defeated by Shouwen.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang met him at Jisu and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 守文單馬立於陳前，泣謂其眾曰：「勿殺吾弟！

translations.literal: Shouwen stood alone on horseback before the battle line and wept, saying to his troops, "Do not kill my younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen rode alone to the front of his line and wept to his men, "Do not kill my younger brother!

sentences.zh: 」守光將元行欽識之，直前擒之，滄德兵皆潰。

translations.literal: " Shouguang's general Yuan Xingqin recognized him, rode straight forward and seized him; the troops of Cang and De all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouguang's general Yuan Xingqin recognized him, charged forward, and seized him; the Cang-De army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 守光囚之別室，栫之藂棘，乘勝進攻滄州。

translations.literal: Shouguang imprisoned him in a separate room and confined him among thorn bushes; pressing his victory, he advanced to attack Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang locked him in a side room and bound him among thorn bushes, then pressed on to attack Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 滄州節度判宮呂兗、孫鶴推守文子延祚為帥，乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Cangzhou military governor's administrative aides Lü Yan and Sun He installed Shouwen's son Yanzuo as commander and manned the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou administrative aides Lü Yan and Sun He installed Shouwen's son Yanzuo as leader and held the walls against him.

sentences.zh: 兗，安次人也。

translations.literal: Yan was a native of Anci.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was from Anci.

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使兼侍中劉知俊，功名浸盛，以帝猜忍日甚，內不自安。

translations.literal: Zhongwu military governor and concurrent palace attendant Liu Zhijun, his fame and achievements gradually flourishing, because the emperor's suspicion and cruelty grew daily, was inwardly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As his fame and achievements grew, Zhongwu military governor and concurrent palace attendant Liu Zhijun grew uneasy—the emperor's suspicion and cruelty were increasing daily.

sentences.zh: 及王重師誅，知俊益懼。

translations.literal: When Wang Chongshi was executed, Zhijun became all the more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongshi was executed, Zhijun's fear only deepened.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐河東，急征知俊入朝，欲以為河東西面行營都統；

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign against Hedong and urgently summoned Zhijun to court, intending to make him overall commander of the western Hedong campaign;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a campaign against Hedong and urgently summoned Zhijun to court, intending to make him overall commander of the western Hedong campaign;

sentences.zh: 且以知俊有丹、延之功，厚賜之。

translations.literal: moreover, because Zhijun had the merit of taking Dan and Yan, he was richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: and because Zhijun had captured Dan and Yan, the emperor rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 知俊弟右保勝指揮使知浣從帝在洛陽，密使人語知俊云：「入必死。

translations.literal: Zhijun's younger brother, Right Baosheng commander Liu Zhihuan, who was with the emperor at Luoyang, secretly sent word to Zhijun, saying, "If you enter court, you will surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun's brother Liu Zhihuan, Right Baosheng commander, was with the emperor at Luoyang and secretly sent word: "If you go to court, you will die.

sentences.zh: 」又白帝，請帥弟侄往迎知俊，帝許之。

translations.literal: " He also reported to the emperor and asked to lead his brothers and nephews to meet Zhijun; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: " He also petitioned the emperor to lead his brothers and nephews to meet Zhijun, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙未朔，知俊奏稱「為軍民所留」，遂以同州附於岐，執監軍及將佐之不從者，皆械送於岐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day yiwei, Zhijun memorialized that he was "detained by the army and the people," and thereupon submitted Tong Prefecture to Qi; he seized the military supervisor and officers who would not follow and sent them all in fetters to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day yiwei, Zhijun reported that he was "held back by soldiers and civilians" and submitted Tong Prefecture to Qi; he seized the military supervisor and officers who refused to follow and sent them in chains to Qi.

sentences.zh: 遣兵襲華州，逐刺史蔡敬思，以兵守潼關。

translations.literal: He sent troops to raid Hua Prefecture, drove out prefect Cai Jingsi, and garrisoned Tong Pass with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops against Hua Prefecture, expelled prefect Cai Jingsi, and posted troops to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 潛遣人以重利啖長安諸將，執劉捍，送於岐，殺之。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent men to entice the generals of Chang'an with heavy bribes; they seized Liu Han and sent him to Qi, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent men to bribe the Chang'an generals with rich rewards; they seized Liu Han, sent him to Qi, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 知俊遣使請兵於岐，亦遣使請晉人出兵攻晉、絳，遺晉王書曰：「不過旬日，可取兩京，復唐社稷。

translations.literal: Zhijun sent envoys to Qi requesting troops and also sent envoys asking Jin to send troops to attack Jin and Jiang prefectures; he wrote to the Prince of Jin, saying, "In no more than ten days the two capitals can be taken and the Tang state restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun asked Qi for troops and also asked Jin to attack Jin and Jiang prefectures; he wrote the Prince of Jin: "Within ten days we can take the two capitals and restore the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 丁未，朔方節度使韓遜奏克鹽城，斬岐所署刺史李繼直。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Shuofang military governor Han Xun reported the capture of Yancheng and the execution of Li Jizhi, whom Qi had appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Shuofang military governor Han Xun reported the capture of Yancheng and the beheading of Li Jizhi, Qi's appointee as prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝遣近臣諭劉知俊曰：「朕待卿甚厚，何忽相負？

translations.literal: The emperor sent a close attendant to instruct Liu Zhijun, saying, "I have treated you very generously—why have you suddenly betrayed me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a close attendant to Liu Zhijun: "I have treated you generously—why have you turned against me?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不背德，但畏族滅如王重師耳。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant does not betray virtue, but I fear extermination of my clan as with Wang Chongshi.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I am not ungrateful, but I fear my clan will be destroyed as Wang Chongshi's was.

sentences.zh: 」帝復使謂之曰：「劉捍言重師陰結邠、岐，朕今悔之無及，捍死不足塞責。

translations.literal: " The emperor again sent word, saying, "Liu Han said Chongshi was secretly in league with Bin and Qi; I now regret it beyond remedy—Han's death is not enough to atone.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent word again: "Liu Han claimed Chongshi was secretly allied with Bin and Qi; I regret that now beyond remedy—Han's death cannot atone for it.

sentences.zh: 」知俊不報。

translations.literal: " Zhijun did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhijun made no answer.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔削知俊官爵，以山南東道節度使楊師厚為西路行營招討使，帥侍衛馬步軍都指揮使劉鄩等討之。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, an edict stripped Zhijun of rank and office; Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou was made western campaign commander, leading palace guard cavalry-and-infantry commander Liu Yan and others against him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict stripped Zhijun of rank and office; Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou was made western campaign commander and led palace guard cavalry-and-infantry commander Liu Yan and others against him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，帝發洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, the emperor set out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor left Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩至潼關東，獲劉知俊伏路兵藺如誨等三十人，釋之使為前導。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan reached east of Tong Pass, he captured thirty of Liu Zhijun's ambush troops including Lin Ruhui and released them to serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan reached a point east of Tong Pass and captured thirty of Liu Zhijun's ambush troops, including Lin Ruhui; he released them to serve as guides.

sentences.zh: 劉知浣迷失道，盤桓數日，乃至關下，關吏納之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhihuan lost his way and wandered for several days before finally reaching the pass; the gate officers admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhihuan lost his way and wandered for days before reaching the pass; the gate officers let him in.

sentences.zh: 如海等繼至，關吏不知其已被擒，亦納之。

translations.literal: Ruhai and the others arrived in succession; the gate officers, not knowing they had already been captured, admitted them as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhai and the others followed; the gate officers, not knowing they had been captured, admitted them too.

sentences.zh: 鄩兵乘門開直進，遂克潼關，追及知浣，擒之。

translations.literal: Yan's troops rushed straight in as the gates opened and thus captured Tong Pass; they pursued and seized Zhihuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's troops burst through the opened gates and took Tong Pass; they pursued and captured Zhihuan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝至陝。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, the emperor reached Shan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the emperor reached Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丹州馬軍都頭王行思等作亂，刺史宋知海逃歸。

translations.literal: Danzhou cavalry commander Wang Xingsi and others mutinied; prefect Song Zhihai fled back home.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhou cavalry commander Wang Xingsi and others rose in mutiny; prefect Song Zhihai fled.

sentences.zh: 帝遣劉知俊侄嗣業持詔指同州招諭知俊，知俊欲輕騎詣行在謝罪，弟知偃止之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Liu Zhijun's nephew Siye with an edict to Tong Prefecture to summon Zhijun; Zhijun wished to ride lightly to the imperial camp to confess guilt, but his younger brother Zhiyan stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhijun's nephew Siye to Tong Prefecture with an edict summoning him; Zhijun wanted to ride lightly to the imperial camp to plead guilty, but his brother Zhiyan dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚等至華州，知俊將聶賞開門降。

translations.literal: When Yang Shihou and the others reached Hua Prefecture, Zhijun's general Nie Shang opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shihou reached Hua Prefecture, Zhijun's general Nie Shang opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 知俊聞潼關不守，官軍繼至，蒼黃失圖，乙卯夜，舉族奔岐。

translations.literal: Hearing that Tong Pass was lost and government troops were arriving in succession, Zhijun, in panic and without a plan, fled with his whole clan to Qi on the night of yimao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Tong Pass had fallen and imperial troops were closing in, Zhijun panicked; on the night of yimao he fled with his entire clan to Qi.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚至長安，岐兵已據城，師厚以奇兵並南山急趨，自西門入，遂克之。

translations.literal: When Yang Shihou reached Chang'an, Qi troops had already occupied the city; Shihou led elite troops along the southern mountains in a forced march, entered through the west gate, and thus recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shihou reached Chang'an, Qi troops already held the city; he led picked troops along the southern hills in a forced march, entered by the west gate, and retook it.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以劉鄩權佑國留後。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Liu Yan was made acting regent of Youguo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Liu Yan was made acting regent of Youguo.

sentences.zh: 岐王厚禮劉知俊，以為中書令。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi treated Liu Zhijun with great courtesy and made him Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi received Liu Zhijun with great honor and made him Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 地狹，無籓鎮處之，但厚給俸祿而已。

translations.literal: The territory was narrow and there was no frontier post for him; he was given only a generous salary.
translations.idiomatic: The domain was too small to grant him a frontier command; he received only a generous stipend.

sentences.zh: 劉守光遣使上表告捷，且言「俟滄德事畢，為陛下掃平並寇。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang sent envoys with a memorial reporting victory and saying, "When the affairs of Cang and De are finished, I will sweep away the bandits of Bing for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang sent a memorial reporting victory and saying, "When Cang and De are settled, I will sweep away the Bing bandits for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」亦致書晉王，雲欲與之同破偽梁。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to the Prince of Jin, saying he wished to join in destroying the false Liang.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote the Prince of Jin offering to join in destroying the usurper Liang.

sentences.zh: 撫州刺史危全諷自稱鎮南節度使，帥撫、信、袁、吉之兵號十萬攻洪州。

translations.literal: Fuzhou prefect Wei Quanfen styled himself Zhennan military governor and led the armies of Fu, Xin, Yuan, and Ji—said to number one hundred thousand—to attack Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou prefect Wei Quanfen styled himself Zhennan military governor and led armies from Fu, Xin, Yuan, and Ji—said to number one hundred thousand—against Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮南守兵才千人，將吏皆懼，節度使劉威密遣使告急於廣陵，日召僚佐宴飲。

translations.literal: Huainan had only a thousand defenders; officers and officials were all afraid; military governor Liu Wei secretly sent messengers to Guangling reporting the emergency while each day summoning staff to banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan had only a thousand defenders; the officers were terrified; military governor Liu Wei secretly sent urgent word to Guangling while each day holding banquets for his staff.

sentences.zh: 全諷聞之，屯象牙潭，不敢進，請兵於楚，楚王殷遣指揮使苑玫會袁州刺史彭彥章圍高安以助全諷。

translations.literal: Quanfen heard of this, encamped at Ivory Pool, and dared not advance; he requested troops from Chu, and King Yin of Chu sent commander Yuan Mei to join Yuanzhou prefect Peng Yanzhang in besieging Gao'an to aid Quanfen.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Quanfen camped at Ivory Pool and hesitated to advance; he asked Chu for aid, and King Ma Yin sent commander Yuan Mei to join Yuanzhou prefect Peng Yanzhang in besieging Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 玫，蔡州人；

translations.literal: Mei was a native of Caizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Mei was from Caizhou;

sentences.zh: 彥章，玕之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhang was a nephew of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang was a nephew of Peng Gan.

sentences.zh: 徐溫問將於嚴可求，可求薦周本。

translations.literal: Xu Wen asked Yan Keqiu for a general; Keqiu recommended Zhou Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen asked Yan Keqiu to recommend a general; Keqiu named Zhou Ben.

sentences.zh: 乃以本為西南面行營招討應援使，將兵七千救高安。

translations.literal: Ben was then made southwestern campaign relief commander and led seven thousand troops to relieve Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was made southwestern campaign relief commander and led seven thousand men to relieve Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 本以前攻蘇州無功，稱疾不出，可求即其臥內強起之。

translations.literal: Because his earlier attack on Suzhou had failed, Ben claimed illness and would not go out; Keqiu forcibly roused him in his bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: Ben had failed at Suzhou and pleaded illness; Keqiu forcibly roused him from his bed.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「蘇州之役，敵不能勝我，但主將權輕耳。

translations.literal: Ben said, "At Suzhou the enemy could not defeat us, but the chief commander lacked authority.
translations.idiomatic: Ben said, "At Suzhou the enemy could not beat us—the problem was that the commander lacked authority.

sentences.zh: 今必見用，願毋置副貳乃可。

translations.literal: If I am truly to be used now, I ask that no deputy be appointed—that alone will do.
translations.idiomatic: If I am to command now, appoint no deputy—that is my condition.

sentences.zh: 」可求許之。

translations.literal: " Keqiu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Keqiu agreed.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「楚人為全諷聲援耳，非欲取高安也。

translations.literal: Ben said, "The Chu men are merely supporting Quanfen—they do not mean to take Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ben said, "The Chu troops are only backing Quanfen—they do not mean to take Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 吾敗全諷，援兵必還。

translations.literal: If we defeat Quanfen, the relief army will surely return.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Quanfen and the relief force will withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」乃疾趣象牙潭。

translations.literal: " He then marched swiftly to Ivory Pool.
translations.idiomatic: " He then marched hard for Ivory Pool.

sentences.zh: 過洪州。

translations.literal: He passed through Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉威欲犒軍，本不肯留。

translations.literal: Liu Wei wished to feast the army; Ben would not stay.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei wanted to feast the troops; Ben refused to stop.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「全諷兵強，君宜觀形勢然後進。

translations.literal: Someone said, "Quanfen's army is strong—you should observe the situation before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged, "Quanfen's force is strong—you should assess the situation before advancing.

sentences.zh: 」本曰：「賊眾十倍於我，我軍聞之必懼，不若乘其銳而用之。

translations.literal: " Ben said, "The bandits outnumber us ten to one; if our troops hear that, they will fear—better to strike while their spirit is high.
translations.idiomatic: " Ben said, "The enemy outnumbers us ten to one; if our men hear that they will lose heart—better to attack while their confidence is still fresh.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子，以劉守光為燕王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiazi, Liu Shouguang was made Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiazi Liu Shouguang was created Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 梁兵克丹州，擒王行思。

translations.literal: Liang troops captured Dan Prefecture and seized Wang Xingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang troops took Dan Prefecture and captured Wang Xingsi.

sentences.zh: 商州刺史李稠驅士民西走，將吏追斬之，推都押牙李玫主州事。

translations.literal: Shangzhou prefect Li Chou drove soldiers and civilians westward in flight; officers pursued and beheaded him and installed chief military adjutant Li Mei to manage the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhou prefect Li Chou drove soldiers and civilians to flee west; officers overtook and killed him and installed chief adjutant Li Mei to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚午，改佑國軍曰永平。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Youguo Army was renamed Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the Youguo Army was renamed Yongping.

sentences.zh: 河東兵寇晉州，抄掠至堯祠而去。

translations.literal: Hedong troops raided Jin Prefecture, plundering as far as Yaoci before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong troops raided Jin Prefecture, looting as far as Yaoci before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝發陝州，乙亥，至洛陽，寢疾。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the emperor set out from Shan Prefecture; on yihai he reached Luoyang and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor left Shan Prefecture; on yihai he reached Luoyang and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 初，帝召山南東道節度使楊師厚，欲使督諸將攻潞州，以前兗海留後王班為留後，鎮襄州。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had summoned Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou, intending to have him supervise the generals in attacking Lu Prefecture; former Yanhai regent Wang Ban was made regent and stationed at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had summoned Shannan East Circuit military governor Yang Shihou to supervise the attack on Lu Prefecture; former Yanhai regent Wang Ban was made regent at Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師厚屢為班言牙兵王求等凶悍，宜備之，班自恃左右有壯士，不以為意，每眾辱之。

translations.literal: Shihou repeatedly told Ban that the garrison soldiers Wang Qiu and others were fierce and should be guarded against; Ban, trusting in the strong men at his side, paid no heed and publicly humiliated them at every gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou repeatedly warned Ban that garrison soldiers Wang Qiu and others were violent and dangerous; Ban, trusting his own strongmen, ignored the warning and publicly humiliated them.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，謫求戍西境，是夕，作亂，殺班，推都指揮使雍丘劉玘為留後。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Qiu was demoted and posted to the western border; that night he mutinied, killed Ban, and installed overall commander Liu Qi of Yongqiu as regent.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Qiu was demoted to the western frontier; that night he mutinied, killed Ban, and installed overall commander Liu Qi of Yongqiu as regent.

sentences.zh: 玘偽從之，明日，與指揮使王延順逃詣帝所。

translations.literal: Qi pretended to accept; the next day he fled with commander Wang Yanshun to the emperor's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Qi feigned acceptance; the next day he fled with commander Wang Yanshun to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 亂兵奉平淮指揮使李洪為留後，附於蜀。

translations.literal: The mutineers installed Pinghuai commander Li Hong as regent and submitted to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers installed Pinghuai commander Li Hong as regent and went over to Shu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，房州刺史楊虔亦叛附於蜀。

translations.literal: Before long, Fangzhou prefect Yang Qian also rebelled and submitted to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fangzhou prefect Yang Qian also rebelled and submitted to Shu.

sentences.zh: 危全諷在象牙潭，營柵臨溪，亙數千里。

translations.literal: Wei Quanfen was at Ivory Pool; his camp palisades lined the stream and stretched for thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Quanfen was at Ivory Pool with palisades along the stream stretching for miles.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，周本隔溪布陳，先使羸兵嘗敵。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Zhou Ben drew up his battle line across the stream and first sent weak troops to probe the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Zhou Ben formed his line across the stream and first sent weak troops to test the enemy.

sentences.zh: 全諷兵涉溪追之，本乘其半濟，縱兵擊之，全諷兵大潰，自相蹂藉，溺水死者甚眾，本分兵斷其歸路，擒全諷及將士五千人。

translations.literal: Quanfen's troops waded the stream in pursuit; Ben, when they were half across, unleashed his troops and struck; Quanfen's army broke utterly, trampling one another; very many drowned; Ben sent detachments to cut off their retreat and captured Quanfen and five thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Quanfen's men waded the stream in pursuit; Ben struck when they were half across; Quanfen's army collapsed in panic, trampling one another; many drowned; Ben cut off their retreat and captured Quanfen and five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 乘勝克袁州，執刺史彭彥章，進攻吉州，歙州刺史陶雅使其子敬昭及都指揮使徐章將兵襲饒、信，信州刺史危仔倡請降，饒州刺史唐寶棄城走。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, he took Yuan Prefecture, seized prefect Peng Yanzhang, and advanced on Ji Prefecture; Shezhou prefect Tao Ya sent his son Jingzhao and overall commander Xu Zhang with troops to raid Rao and Xin; Xinzhou prefect Wei Zaichang offered to surrender, and Raozhou prefect Tang Bao abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on, he took Yuan Prefecture and captured prefect Peng Yanzhang, then advanced on Ji; Shezhou prefect Tao Ya sent his son Jingzhao and overall commander Xu Zhang to raid Rao and Xin; Xinzhou prefect Wei Zaichang surrendered and Raozhou prefect Tang Bao fled.

sentences.zh: 行營都指揮使米志誠、都尉呂師造等敗苑玫於上高。

translations.literal: Campaign overall commander Mi Zhicheng and commander Lü Shizao defeated Yuan Mei at Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commander Mi Zhicheng and commander Lü Shizao defeated Yuan Mei at Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 吉州刺史彭玕帥眾數千人奔楚，楚王殷表玕為郴州刺史，為子希範娶其女。

translations.literal: Jizhou prefect Peng Gan led several thousand men to flee to Chu; King Yin of Chu memorialized Gan as Chenzhou prefect and had his son Xifan marry Gan's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou prefect Peng Gan fled to Chu with several thousand men; King Ma Yin petitioned to make him Chenzhou prefect and had his son Xifan marry Gan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 淮南以左先鋒指揮使張景思知信州，遣行營都虞候骨言將兵五千送之。

translations.literal: Huainan made Left Vanguard commander Zhang Jingsi prefect of Xin and sent campaign deputy commander Guyán with five thousand troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan made Left Vanguard commander Zhang Jingsi prefect of Xin and sent campaign deputy commander Guyán with five thousand men to escort him.

sentences.zh: 危仔倡聞兵至，奔吳越，吳越王鏐以仔倡為淮南節度副使，更其姓曰元氏。

translations.literal: When Wei Zaichang heard troops were coming, he fled to Wuyue; King Qian Liu made Zaichang Huainan deputy military governor and changed his surname to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zaichang heard troops were approaching, he fled to Wuyue; King Qian Liu made him Huainan deputy military governor and changed his surname to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 危全諷至廣陵，弘農王以其嘗有德於武忠王，釋之，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: When Wei Quanfen reached Guangling, the King of Hongnong, because he had once shown favor to the Prince of Wuzhong, released him and supplied him generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Quanfen reached Guangling, the King of Hongnong released him—Quanfen had once aided the Prince of Wuzhong—and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 八月，虔州刺史盧光稠以州附於淮南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qianzhou prefect Lu Guangchou submitted his prefecture to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Qianzhou prefect Lu Guangchou submitted his prefecture to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 於是江西之地盡入於楊氏。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the lands of Jiangxi came under the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all of Jiangxi fell to the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 光稠亦遣使附於梁。

translations.literal: Guangchou also sent envoys submitting to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchou also sent envoys submitting to Liang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上疾小瘳，始復視朝。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, the emperor's illness eased slightly and he resumed holding court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor's illness eased and he resumed holding court.

sentences.zh: 以鎮國節度使康懷貞為西路行營副招討使。

translations.literal: Zhenguo military governor Kang Huaizhen was made deputy western campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguo military governor Kang Huaizhen was made deputy western campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 蜀主命太子宗懿判六軍，開永和府，妙選朝士為僚屬。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler ordered Crown Prince Zongyi to oversee the Six Armies, opened the Yonghe Office, and carefully selected court officials as staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler ordered Crown Prince Zongyi to oversee the Six Armies, opened the Yonghe Office, and carefully selected court officials for his staff.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，均州刺史張敬方奏克房州。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Junzhou prefect Zhang Jingfang reported the capture of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Junzhou prefect Zhang Jingfang reported the capture of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 岐王欲遣劉知俊將兵攻靈、夏，且約晉王使攻晉、絳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi wished to send Liu Zhijun with troops to attack Ling and Xia and also arranged with the Prince of Jin to attack Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi planned to send Liu Zhijun against Ling and Xia and coordinated with the Prince of Jin to attack Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 晉王引兵南下，先遣周德威等將兵出陰地關攻晉州，刺史邊繼威悉力固守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin led troops south; he first sent Zhou Dewei and others with troops out through Yindi Pass to attack Jin Prefecture; prefect Bian Jiwei defended with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin marched south, first sending Zhou Dewei through Yindi Pass against Jin Prefecture; prefect Bian Jiwei defended with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 晉兵穿地道，陷城二十餘步，城中血戰拒之，一夕城復成。

translations.literal: Jin troops dug a tunnel and breached the wall for more than twenty paces; the city fought a bloody battle to resist; in one night the wall was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops tunneled under the wall and breached it for more than twenty paces; the defenders fought a bloody battle; overnight the wall was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 詔楊師厚將兵救晉州，周德威以騎扼蒙坑之險，師厚擊破之，進抵晉州，晉兵解圍遁去。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Shihou to lead troops to relieve Jin Prefecture; Zhou Dewei with cavalry held the defiles of Mengkeng; Shihou broke through and advanced to Jin Prefecture; the Jin troops lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yang Shihou to relieve Jin Prefecture; Zhou Dewei's cavalry held Mengkeng Pass; Shihou broke through and reached Jin Prefecture; the Jin army lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李洪寇荊南，高季昌遣其將倪可福擊敗之。

translations.literal: Li Hong raided Jingnan; Gao Jichang sent his general Ni Kefu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong raided Jingnan; Gao Jichang sent his general Ni Kefu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 詔馬步都指揮使陳暉將兵會荊南兵討洪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered cavalry-and-infantry commander Chen Hui to lead troops to join Jingnan forces in attacking Hong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered cavalry-and-infantry commander Chen Hui to join Jingnan troops against Hong.

sentences.zh: 蜀主以御史中丞王鍇為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler made censor-in-chief Wang Kai Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler made censor-in-chief Wang Kai Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 陳暉軍至襄州，李洪逆戰，大敗，王求死。

translations.literal: When Chen Hui's army reached Xiang Prefecture, Li Hong met him in battle and was utterly defeated; Wang Qiu died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Hui reached Xiang Prefecture, Li Hong gave battle and was crushed; Wang Qiu was killed.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁酉，拔其城，斬叛兵千人，執李洪、楊虔等送洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingyou, the city was taken; a thousand mutineers were beheaded; Li Hong, Yang Qian, and others were seized and sent to Luoyang and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingyou the city fell; a thousand mutineers were beheaded; Li Hong, Yang Qian, and others were sent to Luoyang and executed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以保義節度使王檀為潞州東面行營招討使。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Baoyi military governor Wang Tan was made eastern Lu Prefecture campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Baoyi military governor Wang Tan was made eastern Lu Prefecture campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 劉守光奏遣其子中軍兵馬使繼威安撫滄州吏民。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang memorialized sending his son, central army horse-and-arms commissioner Liu Jiwei, to pacify the officials and people of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang memorialized sending his son, central army horse-and-arms commissioner Liu Jiwei, to pacify Cangzhou's officials and people.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以繼威為義昌留後。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Jiwei was made regent of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Jiwei was made regent of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，侍中韓建罷守太保，左僕射、同平章事楊涉罷守本官。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Palace Attendant Han Jian was demoted to Grand Mentor while retaining his title; Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and co-equal chief minister Yang She was demoted to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Palace Attendant Han Jian was demoted to Grand Mentor; Left Vice Director Yang She was reduced to his original rank.

sentences.zh: 以太常卿趙光逢為中書侍郎，翰林奉旨工部侍郎杜曉為戶部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices director Zhao Guangfeng was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Ministry of Works drafting academician Du Xiao was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue—both as co-equal chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices director Zhao Guangfeng was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and drafting academician Du Xiao of the Ministry of Works was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue—both as co-equal chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 曉，讓能之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao was a son of Rangneng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was a son of Du Rangneng.

sentences.zh: 淮南遣使者張知遠修好於福建，知遠倨慢，閩王審知斬之，表上其書，始與淮南絕。

translations.literal: Huainan sent envoy Zhang Zhiyuan to establish friendly relations with Fujian; Zhiyuan was arrogant and insolent; Prince of Min Wang Shenzhi beheaded him, forwarded his letter to the throne, and broke with Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan sent envoy Zhang Zhiyuan to open relations with Fujian; Zhiyuan was arrogant; Prince of Min Wang Shenzhi executed him, forwarded his letter to the throne, and broke with Huainan.

sentences.zh: 審知性儉約，常躡麻屨，府捨卑陋，未嘗營葺。

translations.literal: Shenzhi was by nature frugal; he often wore hemp sandals; his government offices were low and shabby and he never repaired them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi was frugal by nature, often wearing hemp sandals; his offices were humble and he never renovated them.

sentences.zh: 寬刑薄賦，公私富實，境內以安。

translations.literal: He lightened punishments and reduced taxes; public and private stores were full; within his borders all was secure.
translations.idiomatic: He eased punishments and lowered taxes; public and private coffers grew full, and his domain was at peace.

sentences.zh: 歲自海道登、萊入貢，沒溺者什四五。

translations.literal: Each year tribute was sent by sea route through Deng and Lai; one or two in ten were lost at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Each year tribute went by sea through Deng and Lai; as many as four or five in ten were lost to the waves.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，蜀司天監胡秀林獻《永昌歷》，行之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiazi, Hu Xiulin, Director of the Astronomy Bureau of Shu, presented the Everlasting Prosperity Calendar, and it was put into use.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, Shu astronomy director Hu Xiulin submitted the Everlasting Prosperity Calendar, and the court adopted it.

sentences.zh: 湖州刺史高澧性凶忍，嘗召州吏議曰：「吾欲盡殺百姓，可乎？

translations.literal: Gao Li, prefect of Huzhou, was by nature cruel and ruthless; he once summoned the prefectural clerks and said, "I wish to kill all the common people—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou prefect Gao Li was vicious by nature; he once called his staff together and asked, "I want to slaughter every commoner in the prefecture—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「如此，則租賦何從出？

translations.literal: " The clerks said, "If we do that, from where will rent and taxes come?
translations.idiomatic: " The clerks replied, "If you do that, where will rent and taxes come from?

sentences.zh: 當擇可殺者殺之耳。

translations.literal: We should simply choose those who deserve killing and kill them."
translations.idiomatic: You should pick out those worth killing and kill them—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」時澧糾民為兵，有言其咨怨者，澧悉集民兵於開元寺，紿雲犒享，入則殺之，死者逾半；

translations.literal: At the time Gao Li was conscripting the people as soldiers; when word came that some resented it, he gathered all the militiamen at Kaiyuan Temple, deceiving them with the promise of a reward feast; once they entered he killed them, and more than half died;
translations.idiomatic: While pressing the people into militia service, Gao Li heard reports of grumbling; he assembled the militia at Kaiyuan Temple under the pretense of a reward feast and slaughtered them once inside—well over half were killed;

sentences.zh: 在外者覺之，縱火作亂。

translations.literal: Those outside realized what was happening, set fires, and rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Those still outside caught on, torched the city, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 澧閉城大索，凡殺三千人。

translations.literal: Gao Li closed the city and searched it thoroughly, killing three thousand people in all.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Li shut the gates and launched a sweeping purge, killing three thousand people.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐欲誅之，戊辰，澧以州叛附於淮南，舉兵焚義和臨平鎮，鏐命指揮使錢鏢討之。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue wanted to execute him; on the day wuchen, Gao Li rebelled with the prefecture and submitted to Huainan, raised troops, and burned the garrisons at Yihe and Linping; Liu ordered commander Qian Biao to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu meant to put him to death; on wuchen Gao Li turned the prefecture over to Huainan, burned Yihe and Linping, and Qian Liu sent commander Qian Biao against him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲午，帝告謝於圜丘；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiawu, the emperor performed a thanksgiving rite at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiawu the emperor offered thanks at the Round Mound Altar;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 鄴王羅紹威得風痺病，上表稱：「魏故大鎮，多外兵，願得有功重臣鎮之，臣乞骸骨歸第。

translations.literal: Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei contracted wind paralysis and submitted a memorial stating, "Wei is a former great garrison with many outside troops; I wish that a meritorious senior minister might be stationed there—I beg to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ye, Luo Shaowei, fell ill with crippling paralysis and memorialized: "Wei was once a great stronghold with many outside troops; I ask that an accomplished senior official hold it—I beg leave to retire."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，撫案動容。

translations.literal: " When the emperor heard this, he struck the desk and was visibly moved.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard this, he struck the table, visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以其子周翰為天雄節度副使，知府事。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, he appointed Shaowei's son Zhouhan deputy military governor of Tianxiong to administer prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he appointed Shaowei's son Zhouhan deputy military governor of Tianxiong to run the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 謂使者曰：「亟歸語而主：為我強飯！

translations.literal: He told the envoy, "Hurry back and tell your lord: Eat heartily for my sake!
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoy, "Go back at once and tell your master to eat well for my sake!

sentences.zh: 如有不可諱，當世世貴爾子孫以相報也。

translations.literal: If the inevitable comes, I shall honor your descendants for generation after generation in recompense.
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should happen, I will exalt your descendants for generations in return.

sentences.zh: 今使周翰領軍府，尚冀爾復愈耳。

translations.literal: Now I have Zhouhan lead the military prefecture; I still hope you will recover."
translations.idiomatic: For now Zhouhan leads the army headquarters, but I still hope you recover."

sentences.zh: 岐王欲取靈州以處劉知俊，且以為牧馬之地，使知俊自將兵攻之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi wished to take Lingzhou to settle Liu Zhijun there and also to use it as pastureland for horses, and sent Zhijun at the head of troops to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi wanted Lingzhou to install Liu Zhijun and use the region as horse pasture, and sent Zhijun to attack it.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使韓遜遣使告急；

translations.literal: Shuofang military governor Han Xun sent envoys to report urgent distress;
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang military governor Han Xun sent messengers reporting dire straits;

sentences.zh: 詔鎮國節度使康懷貞、感化節度使寇彥卿將兵攻邠寧以救之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhenguo military governor Kang Huaizhen and Ganhua military governor Kou Yanqing to lead troops to attack Bin and Ning to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhenguo military governor Kang Huaizhen and Ganhua military governor Kou Yanqing to march against Bin and Ning to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 懷貞等所向皆捷，克寧、衍二州，拔慶州南城，刺史李彥廣出降。

translations.literal: Huaizhen and the others were victorious wherever they went, capturing Ning and Yan prefectures, taking the southern city of Qing Prefecture; prefect Li Yanguang came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen's forces won at every turn, taking Ning and Yan and capturing the southern quarter of Qing Prefecture, where prefect Li Yanguang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遊兵侵掠及涇州之境，劉知俊聞之，十二月，己丑，解靈州圍，引兵還。

translations.literal: Roving troops raided as far as the borders of Jing Prefecture; when Liu Zhijun heard this, on the day jichou in the twelfth month he lifted the siege of Lingzhou and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Raider columns pushed to the borders of Jing Prefecture; hearing this, on jichou in the twelfth month Liu Zhijun broke off the siege of Lingzhou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝急召懷貞等還，遣兵迎援於三原青谷。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently recalled Huaizhen and the others and dispatched troops to meet and reinforce them at Qinggu near Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurriedly recalled Huaizhen and sent troops to meet them at Qinggu near Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 懷貞等還，至三水，知俊遣兵據險邀之，左龍驤軍使壽張王彥章力戰，懷貞等乃得過。

translations.literal: As Huaizhen and the others were returning and reached Sanshui, Zhijun sent troops to hold the high ground and intercept them; Wang Yanzhang of Shouzhang, Left Dragon Courage Army commissioner, fought fiercely, and only then were they able to get through.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanshui on the return march, Zhijun's men seized the passes; Wang Yanzhang of Shouzhang, Left Dragon Courage commander, fought desperately, and Huaizhen's column barely broke through.

sentences.zh: 懷貞與裨將李德遇、許從實、王審權分道而行，皆與援兵不相值，至昇平，劉知俊伏兵山口，懷貞大敗，僅以身免，德遇等軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Huaizhen and subordinate generals Li Deyu, Xu Congshi, and Wang Shenquan took separate routes, none meeting the relief troops; at Shengping, Liu Zhijun ambushed them at a mountain pass; Huaizhen was utterly defeated and barely escaped; the armies of Deyu and the others were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen split with subordinates Li Deyu, Xu Congshi, and Wang Shenquan, each taking a different road and missing the relief force; at Shengping Liu Zhijun ambushed them at a pass—Huaizhen escaped alone while Deyu and the others were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 岐王以知俊為彰義節度使，鎮涇州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi appointed Zhijun Zhangyi military governor, stationed at Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi made Zhijun Zhangyi military governor and posted him at Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王彥章驍勇絕倫，每戰用二鐵槍，皆重百斤，一置鞍中，一在手，所向無前，時人謂之「王鐵槍」。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang's martial valor was unmatched; in every battle he used two iron spears, each weighing a hundred jin—one in his saddle, one in his hand—and swept all before him; people called him "Iron Spear Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang was peerlessly fierce; he fought with two iron spears of a hundred jin each—one in his saddle, one in hand—and cut down everything in his path; men called him Iron Spear Wang.

sentences.zh: 蜀蜀州刺史王宗弁稱疾，罷歸成都，杜門不出。

translations.literal: Wang Zongbian, Shu prefect of Suizhou, claimed illness, left his post and returned to Chengdu, and shut his doors.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Suizhou prefect Wang Zongbian pleaded illness, resigned, returned to Chengdu, and shut himself indoors.

sentences.zh: 蜀主疑其矜功怨望，加檢校太保，固辭不受，謂人曰：「廉者足而不憂，貪者憂而不足。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler suspected him of boasting of his merits and harboring resentment, promoted him to honorary Grand Guardian, but Zongbian firmly declined, telling people, "The honest man has enough and does not worry; the greedy man worries though he never has enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler suspected pride and simmering resentment, tried to promote him to honorary Grand Guardian, but Zongbian refused, saying, "The honest man has enough and does not worry; the greedy man worries though he never has enough.

sentences.zh: 吾小人，致位至此，足矣，豈可求進不已乎！

translations.literal: I am a petty man who has risen to this rank—that is enough; how could I seek advancement without end!
translations.idiomatic: I am a nobody who has risen this high—that is enough; how could I keep grasping for more!

sentences.zh: 」蜀主嘉其志而許之，賜與有加。

translations.literal: " The Shu ruler admired his resolve and granted his request, bestowing gifts in addition.
translations.idiomatic: " The Shu ruler admired his restraint, granted his wish, and heaped gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 劉守光圍滄州久不下，執劉守文至城下示之，猶固守。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang besieged Cangzhou for a long time without taking it; he brought Liu Shouwen beneath the walls to show him, yet the city still held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang besieged Cangzhou for a long time; he dragged Liu Shouwen to the foot of the walls, yet the defenders still held out.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，民食堇泥，軍士食人，驢馬相啖□□尾。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; the people ate akē mud; the soldiers ate human flesh; donkeys and horses devoured one another, even gnawing each other's tails.
translations.idiomatic: The city's food ran out; civilians ate akē mud; soldiers ate human flesh; donkeys and horses fed on one another, gnawing each other's tails.

sentences.zh: 呂兗選男女羸弱者，飼以麴面而烹之，以給軍食，謂之宰殺務。

translations.literal: Lü Yan selected weak men and women, fed them with flour and then boiled them to supply army rations—this was called the Butchery Office.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yan picked the weakest men and women, fattened them on flour and cooked them to feed the army—a practice called the Butchery Office.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未，劉延祚力盡出降。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yimei, Liu Yanzuo, his strength exhausted, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yimei Liu Yanzuo, spent at last, came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時劉繼威尚幼，守光使大將張萬進、周知裕輔之鎮滄州，以延祚及其將佐歸幽州，族呂兗而釋孫鶴。

translations.literal: Liu Jiwei was still young; Shouguang had great generals Zhang Wanjin and Zhou Zhiyu assist him in governing Cangzhou, sent Yanzuo and his officers back to Youzhou, executed Lü Yan's entire clan, and released Sun He.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei was still a child; Shouguang had Zhang Wanjin and Zhou Zhiyu help him hold Cangzhou, sent Yanzuo and his officers to Youzhou, wiped out Lü Yan's clan, and freed Sun He.

sentences.zh: 兗子琦，年十五，門下客趙玉紿監刑者曰：「此吾弟也，勿妄殺。

translations.literal: Lü Yan's son Qi, fifteen years old—a retainer Zhao Yu deceived the execution supervisor, saying, "This is my younger brother; do not kill him rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yan's son Qi was fifteen; client Zhao Yu tricked the execution overseer: "This is my younger brother—do not kill him by mistake.

sentences.zh: 」監刑者信之，遂挈以逃。

translations.literal: " The supervisor believed him and seized the boy to flee.
translations.idiomatic: " The overseer believed him and snatched the boy away.

sentences.zh: 琦足痛不能行，玉負之，變姓名，乞食於路，僅而得免。

translations.literal: Qi's feet hurt and he could not walk; Yu carried him, changed their names, begged for food along the road, and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's feet were too sore to walk; Yu carried him, changed their names, begged along the roads, and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 琦感家門殄滅，力學自立，晉王聞其名，署代州判官。

translations.literal: Moved by the annihilation of his family, Qi studied diligently; when the Prince of Jin heard his name, he appointed him administrative aide of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving his family's destruction, Qi threw himself into study; the Prince of Jin heard of him and made him judge-advocate of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以盧光稠為鎮南留後。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Lu Guangchou was appointed acting military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Lu Guangchou was made acting military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 劉守光為其父仁恭請致仕，丙午，以仁恭為太師，致仕。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang requested retirement for his father Rengong; on the day bingwu, Rengong was made Grand Preceptor and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang petitioned for his father Rengong to retire; on bingwu Rengong was named Grand Preceptor and stepped down.

sentences.zh: 守光尋使人潛殺其兄守文，歸罪於殺者而誅之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Shouguang secretly had his elder brother Shouwen killed, blamed the assassins, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shouguang secretly had Shouwen murdered, pinned the crime on the killers, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 二月，萬全感自岐歸廣陵，岐王承製加弘農王兼中書令，嗣吳王，於是吳王赦其境內。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wan Quangan returned from Qi to Guangling; the Prince of Qi, following imperial appointment, promoted the King of Hongnong to concurrent Director of the Secretariat and successor as Prince of Wu; the Prince of Wu then granted amnesty within his territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wan Quangan returned from Qi to Guangling; the Prince of Qi elevated the King of Hongnong to Director of the Secretariat and heir as Prince of Wu, who then proclaimed amnesty throughout his domain.

sentences.zh: 高澧求救於吳，吳常州刺史李簡等將兵應之，湖州將盛師友、沈行思閉城不內；

translations.literal: Gao Li sought rescue from Wu; Changzhou prefect Li Jian of Wu and others led troops to respond; Huzhou generals Sheng Shiyou and Shen Xingsi closed the city and would not admit them;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Li asked Wu for help; Wu's Changzhou prefect Li Jian marched out, but Huzhou generals Sheng Shiyou and Shen Xingsi shut the gates and refused entry;

sentences.zh: 澧帥麾下五千人奔吳。

translations.literal: Gao Li led five thousand men under his command and fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Li took his five thousand followers and fled into Wu.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸巳，吳越王鏐巡湖州，以錢鏢為刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day guisi, King Qian Liu of Wuyue inspected Huzhou and appointed Qian Biao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guisi King Qian Liu toured Huzhou and installed Qian Biao as prefect.

sentences.zh: 蜀太子宗懿驕暴，好陵傲舊臣。
