translations.literal: The Shu crown prince Zongyi was arrogant and violent, fond of humiliating old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shu crown prince Zongyi was proud and brutal and loved to bully veteran officials.

sentences.zh: 內樞密使唐道襲，蜀主之嬖臣也，太子屢謔之於朝，由是有隙，互相訴於蜀主。

translations.literal: Tang Daoxi, Commissioner of Palace Affairs, was a favored minister of the Shu ruler; the crown prince repeatedly mocked him at court; because of this there was a rift, and each complained to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Affairs commissioner Tang Daoxi was a Shu favorite; the crown prince repeatedly ridiculed him at court until each went to the ruler with complaints.

sentences.zh: 蜀主恐其交惡，以道襲為山南西道節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler, fearing open hostility, made Daoxi Shannan West Circuit military governor and concurrent co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing open enmity, the Shu ruler posted Daoxi to Shannan West Circuit as military governor and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 道襲薦宣徽北院使鄭頊為內樞密使，頊受命之日，即欲按道襲昆弟盜用內庫金帛。

translations.literal: Daoxi recommended Northern Privy Secretariat commissioner Zheng Xu as Commissioner of Palace Affairs; on the day Xu received appointment he immediately sought to investigate Daoxi's brothers for embezzling from the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi recommended Northern Privy Secretariat commissioner Zheng Xu to succeed him; the day Xu took office he moved to investigate Daoxi's brothers for stealing from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 道襲懼，奏項褊急，不可大任，丙午，出頊為果州刺史，以宣徽南院使潘炕為內樞密使。

translations.literal: Daoxi grew afraid and memorialized that Xu was narrow-minded and impetuous, unfit for a major post; on the day bingwu, Xu was sent out as prefect of Guo Prefecture, and Southern Privy Secretariat commissioner Pan Kang was made Commissioner of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Daoxi memorialized that Xu was narrow and rash; on bingwu Xu was demoted to Guo Prefecture and Pan Kang of the Southern Privy Secretariat was named Commissioner of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏州都指揮使高宗益作亂，殺節度使李彝昌。

translations.literal: Xia Prefecture chief commander Gao Zongyi rebelled and killed military governor Li Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Prefecture chief commander Gao Zongyi rose in revolt and killed military governor Li Yichang.

sentences.zh: 將吏共誅宗益，推彝昌族父蕃漢都指揮使李仁福為帥，癸丑，仁福以聞。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks jointly executed Zongyi and recommended Li Renfu, Yichang's clansman and Fan-Han chief commander, as commander; on the day guichou, Renfu reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Officers killed Zongyi together and chose Yichang's clansman Li Renfu, Fan-Han chief commander, as leader; on guichou Renfu reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，以仁福為定難節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiazi, Renfu was appointed Dingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi Renfu was appointed Dingnan military governor.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，宋州節度使衡王友諒獻瑞麥，一莖三穗，帝曰：「豐年為上瑞。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Prince of Heng You Liang, Songzhou military governor, presented auspicious wheat with three ears on one stalk; the emperor said, "An abundant harvest is the supreme auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Prince of Heng You Liang, Songzhou military governor, presented auspicious wheat with three heads on one stalk; the emperor said, "A bountiful harvest is the greatest good omen.

sentences.zh: 今宋州大水，安用此為！

translations.literal: Now Songzhou suffers great floods—what use is this!
translations.idiomatic: Songzhou is drowning in flood—what good is this!

sentences.zh: 」詔除本縣令名，遣使詰責友諒，以兗海留後惠王友能代為宋州留後。

translations.literal: " An edict removed the local magistrate's name, dispatched envoys to rebuke You Liang, and had Prince of Hui You Neng, Yanhai regent, replace him as Songzhou regent.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the magistrate's name struck from the record, rebuked You Liang, and replaced him with Prince of Hui You Neng as Songzhou regent.

sentences.zh: 友諒、友能，皆全昱子也。

translations.literal: You Liang and You Neng were both sons of Quanyu.
translations.idiomatic: You Liang and You Neng were both sons of Quanyu.

sentences.zh: 帝以晉州刺史下邑華溫琪拒晉兵有功，欲賞之，會護國節度使冀王友謙上言晉、絳邊河東，乞別建節鎮，壬申，以晉、絳、沁三州為定昌軍，以溫琪為節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to reward Xiayi prefect Hua Wenqi of Jin Prefecture for resisting Jin troops; Prince of Ji You Qian, Huguo military governor, memorialized that Jin and Jiang bordered Hedong and requested a separate commission; on the day renshen, Jin, Jiang, and Qin were made the Dingchang Army, with Wenqi as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to reward Jin Prefecture's Hua Wenqi of Xiayi for holding off Jin; Prince of Ji You Qian argued Jin and Jiang lay on the Hedong frontier; on renshen Jin, Jiang, and Qin became the Dingchang Army under Wenqi.

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍寇彥卿入朝，至天津橋，有民不避道，投諸欄外而死。

translations.literal: Left Golden Warriors grand general Kou Yanqing came to court; at Tianjin Bridge a commoner failed to yield the way; Yanqing threw him over the railing and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Left Golden Warriors grand general Kou Yanqing came to court; at Tianjin Bridge a commoner failed to clear the road and Yanqing had him thrown over the railing to his death.

sentences.zh: 彥卿自首於帝。

translations.literal: Yanqing surrendered himself to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing turned himself in.

sentences.zh: 帝以彥卿才幹有功，久在左右。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Yanqing talented and meritorious and long in his personal service,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Yanqing was capable and had long served at his side,

sentences.zh: 命以私財遺死者家以贖罪。

translations.literal: ordered him to compensate the deceased's family from private funds to atone for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: ordered him to pay the dead man's family from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 御史司憲崔沂劾奏「彥卿殺人闕下，請論如法。

translations.literal: Censorate director Cui Yi impeached: "Yanqing killed a man at the palace gate—please punish according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate director Cui Yi impeached him: "Yanqing killed a man at the palace gate—punish him by law.

sentences.zh: 」帝命彥卿分析。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Yanqing to explain.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Yanqing to answer.

sentences.zh: 彥卿對：「令從者舉置欄外，不意誤死。

translations.literal: Yanqing replied, "I ordered my attendants to lift him over the railing; I did not expect he would die.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing replied, "I told my followers to lift him over the railing—I never meant for him to die.

sentences.zh: 」帝欲以過失論，沂奏：「在法，以勢使令為首，下手為從，不得歸罪從者；

translations.literal: " The emperor wished to treat it as accidental; Yi memorialized, "By law, he who commands by authority is the principal and he who carries out the act is the accessory—one cannot shift blame to subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wanted to treat it as accident; Yi argued: "Under law whoever gives the order is the principal and whoever carries it out is the accessory—you cannot shift blame to followers;

sentences.zh: 不鬥而故毆傷人，加傷罪一等，不得為過失。

translations.literal: striking and injuring someone without mutual combat adds one degree to the assault charge—it cannot be treated as accident.
translations.idiomatic: Striking without mutual combat adds a degree to the assault charge—that is not accidental harm.

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，責授彥卿游擊將軍、左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: " On the day xinsi, Yanqing was demoted to Mobile General and Left Guard Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinsi Yanqing was demoted to Mobile General and Left Guard Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 彥卿揚言：「有得崔沂首者，賞錢萬緡。

translations.literal: Yanqing proclaimed publicly, "Whoever brings me Cui Yi's head shall receive ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing announced, "Ten thousand strings of cash to whoever brings me Cui Yi's head.

sentences.zh: 」沂以白帝，帝使人謂彥卿：「崔沂有毫髮傷，我當族汝！

translations.literal: " Yi reported this to the emperor; the emperor sent word to Yanqing, "If Cui Yi suffers even a hair's breadth of harm, I will exterminate your clan!
translations.idiomatic: " Yi reported this; the emperor warned Yanqing, "If Cui Yi loses so much as a hair, I will wipe out your whole clan!

sentences.zh: 」時功臣驕橫，由是稍肅，沂，沆之弟也。

translations.literal: " At the time meritorious ministers were arrogant; from this they became somewhat subdued; Yi was the younger brother of Cui Hang.
translations.idiomatic: " The merit-holders were swaggering; after this they quieted down; Yi was Cui Hang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳徐溫母周氏卒，將吏致祭，為偶人，高數尺，衣以羅錦，溫曰：「此皆出民力，奈何施於此而焚之，宜解以衣貧者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zhou, mother of Xu Wen of Wu, died; officers made offerings, crafting effigies several feet tall clothed in silk brocade; Wen said, "These all come from the people's labor—how can we use them thus and burn them? Better to unstitch them and clothe the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xu Wen's mother Zhou died; officers made funeral effigies dressed in brocade; Wen said, "All this was wrung from the people—why waste it here only to burn it? Give the cloth to the poor.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，起復為內外馬步軍都軍使，領潤州觀察使。

translations.literal: " Before long he was recalled from mourning to serve as commander-in-chief of all internal and external cavalry and infantry, concurrently Runzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was recalled to command all horse and foot forces and hold Runzhou governorship.

sentences.zh: 岐王屢求貨於蜀，蜀主皆與之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi repeatedly asked Shu for goods, and the Shu ruler gave him everything.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi kept asking Shu for goods, and the Shu ruler gave whatever he wanted.

sentences.zh: 又求巴、劍二州，蜀主曰：「吾奉茂貞，勤亦至矣；

translations.literal: He also asked for Ba and Jian prefectures; the Shu ruler said, "In serving Maozhen, my diligence has already been utmost;
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded Ba and Jian; the Shu ruler said, "I have already done all I can for Maozhen;

sentences.zh: 若與之地，是棄民也，寧多與之貨。

translations.literal: if I cede territory, that is abandoning the people; better to give him more goods instead.
translations.idiomatic: To hand over territory would abandon the people—I would rather send more goods.

sentences.zh: 」乃復以絲、茶、布、帛七萬遺之。

translations.literal: " He again sent him seventy thousand measures of silk, tea, cloth, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent another seventy thousand measures of silk, tea, cloth, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以劉繼威為義昌節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Liu Jiwei was appointed Yichang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Liu Jiwei was made Yichang military governor.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，天雄節度使兼中書令鄴貞莊王羅紹威卒。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Prince of Ye Zhenzhuang Luo Shaowei, Tianxiong military governor and concurrent Secretariat director, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Luo Shaowei, Prince of Ye Zhenzhuang, Tianxiong military governor and Secretariat director, died.

sentences.zh: 詔以其子周翰為天雄留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed his son Zhouhan as Tianxiong regent.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed his son Zhouhan Tianxiong regent.

sentences.zh: 匡國節度使長樂忠敬王馮行襲疾篤，表請代者。

translations.literal: Prince of Changle Zhongjing Feng Xingxi, Kuangguo military governor, fell gravely ill and requested a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi, Prince of Changle Zhongjing and Kuangguo military governor, fell gravely ill and asked to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 許州牙兵二千，皆秦宗權餘黨，帝深以為憂。

translations.literal: Two thousand Xuzhou garrison troops were all remnants of Qin Zongquan's faction; the emperor was deeply concerned.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Xuzhou garrison troops were Qin Zongquan holdovers, and the emperor was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚戌，命崇政院直學士李珽馳往視行襲病，曰：「善諭朕意，勿使亂我近鎮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengxu, the emperor ordered Chongzheng Academy academician Li Ting to hurry to visit Xingxi's illness, saying, "Explain my intentions well—do not let disorder arise in my nearby garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengxu the emperor sent Chongzheng academician Li Ting posthaste to Xingxi, saying, "Make my wishes clear—do not let nearby garrisons fall into chaos.

sentences.zh: 」珽至許州，謂將吏曰：「天子握百萬兵，去此數捨耳；

translations.literal: " When Ting reached Xuzhou, he told the officers, "The Son of Heaven holds a million troops, only a few dozen li from here;
translations.idiomatic: " At Xuzhou Ting told the officers, "The Son of Heaven commands a million soldiers only a few dozen li away;

sentences.zh: 馮公忠純，勿使上有所疑。

translations.literal: Lord Feng is loyal and pure—do not let the throne harbor suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Feng is loyal through and through—do not give the throne reason to doubt.

sentences.zh: 汝曹赤心奉國，何憂不富貴！

translations.literal: You who serve the state with honest hearts—why worry you will not gain wealth and rank!
translations.idiomatic: Serve the state with honest hearts—what need to fear missing wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: 」由是眾莫敢異議。

translations.literal: " Therefore none dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: " After that no one objected.

sentences.zh: 行襲欲使人代受詔，珽曰：「東首加朝服，禮也。

translations.literal: Xingxi wished to have someone receive the edict on his behalf; Ting said, "Facing east in court dress—that is the proper rite.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi wanted someone to receive the edict for him; Ting said, "To face east in court dress is the proper rite.

sentences.zh: 」乃即臥內宣詔，謂行襲曰：「公善自輔養，勿視事，此子孫之福也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the edict was proclaimed in his sickbed; Ting told Xingxi, "Take good care of yourself and do not attend to affairs—that is fortune for your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was read in his sickroom; Ting said, "Look after yourself and leave affairs alone—that blesses your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」行襲泣謝，遂解兩使印授珽，使代掌軍府。

translations.literal: " Xingxi wept in thanks, then relinquished both commissioner's seals to Ting to administer the military prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingxi wept his thanks and handed both commissioner seals to Ting to run headquarters.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之曰：「予固知珽能辦事，馮族亦不亡矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he said, "I knew Ting could handle this; the Feng clan will not perish after all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I knew Ting could manage this—the Feng line will not die out.

sentences.zh: 」庚辰，行襲卒。

translations.literal: " On the day gengchen, Xingxi died.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengchen Xingxi died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以李珽權知匡國留後，悉以行襲兵分隸諸校，冒馮姓者皆還宗。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Li Ting was appointed acting Kuangguo regent; all of Xingxi's troops were distributed among commanders; those who had taken the Feng surname returned to their original clans.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Li Ting was made acting Kuangguo regent; Xingxi's soldiers were split among commanders and everyone who had taken the Feng surname reverted to his own clan.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷求為天策上將，詔加天策上將軍。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu requested appointment as Grand Strategist General; an edict added that title.
translations.idiomatic: King Ma Yin asked to be Grand Strategist General, and the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 殷始開天策府，以弟賨為左相，存為右相。

translations.literal: Yin then established the Grand Strategist Office, appointing his younger brothers Cong as Left Chancellor and Cun as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Yin opened the Grand Strategist Office, naming brothers Cong left chancellor and Cun right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 殷遣將侵荊南，軍於油口。

translations.literal: Yin sent generals to invade Jingnan and encamped at Youkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent generals against Jingnan and camped at Youkou.

sentences.zh: 高季昌擊破之，斬首五千級，逐北至白田而還。

translations.literal: Gao Jichang defeated them, beheaded five thousand, pursued them north to Baitian, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jichang routed them, took five thousand heads, chased them to Baitian, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吳水軍指揮使敖駢圍吉州刺史彭玕弟瑊於赤石，楚兵救瑊，虜駢以歸。

translations.literal: Wu naval commander Ao Pian besieged Jian, younger brother of Jizhou prefect Peng Gan, at Chishi; Chu troops rescued Jian, captured Pian, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu naval commander Ao Pian besieged Peng Gan's brother Jian at Chishi; Chu forces relieved Jian, captured Pian, and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子朔，蜀門下侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事韌城卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the month (wuzi), Wei Zhaoyuan, Deputy Director of the Chancellery, concurrent Minister of Personnel, and co-equal chief minister of Shu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of wuzi, Wei Zhaoyuan—deputy director of the chancellery, minister of personnel, and co-equal chief minister of Shu—died.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐表「宦者周延誥等二十五人，唐末避禍至此，非劉、韓之黨，乞原之。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue memorialized, "The eunuchs Zhou Yanhao and twenty-four others came here fleeing disaster at the end of Tang; they are not partisans of Liu or Han; we beg that they be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue submitted a memorial: "The eunuchs Zhou Yanhao and twenty-four others fled here at the end of the Tang to escape calamity; they are not partisans of the Liu or Han factions—we ask that they be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此屬吾知其無罪，但今革弊之初，不欲置之禁掖，可且留於彼，諭以此意。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "These people—I know they are guiltless, but now at the beginning of reform, I do not wish to place them in the forbidden precincts; they may for now be kept where they are, and this intention may be conveyed to them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "I know these men are innocent, but at the outset of reform I do not mean to bring them into the inner palace; let them remain where they are for now and explain that to them.

sentences.zh: 岐王與邠、涇二帥各遣使告晉，請合兵攻定難節度使李仁福。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi and the military governors of Bin and Jing each sent envoys to inform Jin, requesting united forces to attack Dingnan military governor Li Renfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi and the commanders of Bin and Jing each sent messengers to Jin to propose a joint campaign against Dingnan military governor Li Renfu.

sentences.zh: 晉王遣振武節度使周德威將兵會之，合五萬眾圍夏州，仁福嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin sent Zhende military governor Zhou Dewei to lead troops to join them; together they gathered fifty thousand men and besieged Xia Prefecture; Renfu closed the city and held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin dispatched Zhende military governor Zhou Dewei at the head of an army to join the allied force; fifty thousand troops surrounded Xia Prefecture, and Renfu shut the gates and defended.

sentences.zh: 八月，以劉守光兼義昌節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Shouguang was additionally appointed military governor of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Shouguang was also made military governor of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 鎮、定自帝踐祚以來雖不輸常賦，而貢獻甚勤。

translations.literal: Zhen and Ding, since the emperor ascended the throne, although they did not remit regular taxes, their tribute offerings were very zealous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Ding had not paid regular taxes since the emperor took the throne, but their tribute gifts had been lavish.

sentences.zh: 會趙王鎔母何氏卒，庚申，遣使吊之，且授起復官。

translations.literal: When the mother of Prince of Zhao Wang Rong, née He, died, on the day gengshen envoys were sent to offer condolences, and he was also granted resumption from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Wang Rong's mother, Lady He, died, the court sent condolences on gengshen and authorized him to leave mourning and resume office.

sentences.zh: 時鄰道弔客皆在館，使者見晉使，歸，言於帝曰：「鎔潛與晉通，鎮、定勢強，終恐難制。

translations.literal: At the time envoys from neighboring circuits offering condolences were all lodged at the guesthouse; an envoy saw Jin envoys; on returning he spoke to the emperor, saying, "Rong is secretly in communication with Jin; Zhen and Ding are strong—in the end we may fear they will be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from neighboring circuits were all lodged in the guesthouse when one of them spotted Jin's messengers; returning, he told the emperor, "Rong is secretly dealing with Jin, and with Zhen and Ding so strong, he may prove impossible to control in the end.

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thought that quite right.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，李仁福來告急。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Li Renfu came to report an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Renfu sent an urgent plea for help.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以河南尹兼中書令張宗奭為西京留守。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Henan governor and concurrent chancellor Zhang Zongshi was made western capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Zhang Zongshi, governor of Henan and chancellor, was appointed western capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 帝恐晉兵襲西京，以宣化留後李思安為東北面行營都指揮使，將兵萬人屯河陽。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that Jin troops would strike the western capital; he made Xuanhua acting governor Li Si'an commander-in-chief of the northeastern field headquarters, leading ten thousand troops to encamp at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a Jin strike on the western capital, the emperor named Xuanhua acting governor Li Si'an commander of the northeastern field headquarters and sent ten thousand men to camp at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，帝發洛陽；

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the emperor set out from Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the emperor left Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 己巳，至陝。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, he reached Shan.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he reached Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以鎮國節度使楊師厚為西路行營招討使，會感化節度使康懷貞將兵三萬屯三原。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Zhenguo military governor Yang Shihou was made commander of the western field headquarters for punitive operations; he joined Ganhuo military governor Kang Huaizhen, leading thirty thousand troops to encamp at Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Zhenguo military governor Yang Shihou was made western field commander, joining Ganhuo military governor Kang Huaizhen with thirty thousand troops at Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝憂晉兵出澤州逼懷州，既而聞其在綏、銀磧中，曰：「無足慮也。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that Jin troops might come out from Ze Prefecture to press Huai Prefecture; soon afterward he heard they were in the wastes of Sui and Yin, and said, "There is nothing worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared Jin might advance from Ze Prefecture toward Huai Prefecture, but then word came they were stuck in the wastes of Sui and Yin. "Nothing to worry about," he said.

sentences.zh: 」甲申，遣夾馬指揮使李遇、劉綰自鄜、延趨銀、夏，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: " On the day jiashen he sent Jiamu commanders Li Yu and Liu Wan from Fu and Yan to hurry toward Yin and Xia and cut off their route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiashen he sent Jiamu commanders Li Yu and Liu Wan from Fu and Yan toward Yin and Xia to cut off the enemy's retreat.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐築捍海石唐，廣杭州城，大修台館。

translations.literal: King Qian Liu of Wuyue built the Stone Tang seawall to hold back the sea, expanded the walls of Hang Prefecture, and greatly repaired pavilions and halls.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue built a stone seawall, enlarged Hangzhou's walls, and lavishly restored pavilions and halls.

sentences.zh: 由是錢唐富庶盛於東南。

translations.literal: From this Qiantang grew rich and prosperous beyond all the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang became the richest and most prosperous place in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 九月，己丑，上發陝；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, the emperor set out from Shan;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jichou, the emperor marched from Shan;

sentences.zh: 甲午，至洛陽，疾復作。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, he reached Luoyang, and his illness recurred.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he reached Luoyang, and his illness flared again.

sentences.zh: 李遇等至夏州，岐、晉兵皆解去。

translations.literal: When Li Yu and the others reached Xia Prefecture, the Qi and Jin armies both dispersed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Yu's force reached Xia Prefecture, the Qi and Jin armies broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，遣鎮國節度楊師厚、相州刺史李思安將兵屯澤州以圖上黨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Zhenguo military governor Yang Shihou and Xiang Prefecture prefect Li Si'an were sent to lead troops to encamp at Ze Prefecture in order to strike at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Yang Shihou of Zhenguo and Li Si'an of Xiangzhou were sent to camp at Ze Prefecture with an eye to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐之巡湖州也，留沈行思為巡檢使，與盛師友俱歸。

translations.literal: When King Qian Liu of Wuyue toured Huzhou, he left Shen Xingsi as inspection commissioner; Xingsi and Sheng Shiyou both returned together.
translations.idiomatic: While King Qian Liu toured Huzhou he left Shen Xingsi as inspection commissioner; Xingsi returned together with Sheng Shiyou.

sentences.zh: 行思謂同列陳瑰曰：「王若以師友為刺史，何以處我？

translations.literal: Xingsi said to his colleague Chen Gui, "If the king appoints Shiyou prefect, how will he deal with me?
translations.idiomatic: Xingsi asked his colleague Chen Gui, "If the king makes Shiyou a prefect, what place will there be for me?

sentences.zh: 」時瑰已得鏐密旨遣行思詣府，乃紿之曰：「何不自詣王所論之！

translations.literal: " At the time Gui had already received Liu's secret order to send Xingsi to the capital, so he deceived him, saying, "Why not go yourself to discuss it with the king!
translations.idiomatic: " Gui had already received Liu's secret order to summon Xingsi to court, so he lied: "Why not go plead your case before the king yourself!

sentences.zh: 」行思從之。

translations.literal: " Xingsi followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingsi took his advice.

sentences.zh: 既至數日，鏐送其家亦至，行思恨鏐賣己。

translations.literal: After several days there, Liu sent for his family, who also arrived; Xingsi resented that Liu had sold him out.
translations.idiomatic: Within days his family was sent for and arrived as well; Xingsi realized Liu had betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 鏐自衣錦軍歸，將吏迎謁，行思取鍛槌擊瑰，殺之，因詣鏐，與師友論功，奪左右槊，欲刺師友，眾執之。

translations.literal: When Liu returned from the Yijin Army, generals and officials came to welcome him; Xingsi seized a forging hammer, struck Gui, and killed him; then he went to Liu, disputing merit with Shiyou; he snatched a spear from a guard and tried to stab Shiyou; the crowd seized him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu returned from the Yijin Army and his officers came out to greet him, Xingsi grabbed a smith's hammer, killed Chen Gui with it, then confronted Liu and Sheng Shiyou over credit for merit; seizing a guard's spear he tried to run Shiyou through, but the bystanders grabbed him.

sentences.zh: 鏐斬行思，以師友為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu executed Xingsi and made Shiyou prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had Xingsi beheaded and appointed Shiyou prefect of Wu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己丑，以寧國節度使、同平章事王景仁充北面行營都指揮招討使，潞州副招討使韓勍副之，以李思安為先鋒將，趣上黨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jichou, Ningguo military governor and co-equal chief minister Wang Jingren was appointed commander-in-chief and punitive commissioner of the northern field headquarters; Lu Prefecture deputy punitive commissioner Han Qing served as his deputy; Li Si'an was made vanguard general, marching toward Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jichou, Ningguo military governor and co-equal chief minister Wang Jingren was named northern field commander; Han Qing of Lu Prefecture served as his deputy; Li Si'an led the vanguard toward Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 尋遣景仁等屯魏州，楊師厚還陝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jingren and the others were sent to encamp at Weizhou; Yang Shihou returned to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jingren's force was posted at Weizhou while Yang Shihou went back to Shan.

sentences.zh: 蜀主更太子宗懿名曰元坦。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler changed the name of crown prince Zongyi to Yuantan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler renamed crown prince Zongyi as Yuantan.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，立假子宗裕為通王，宗范為夔王，宗金歲為昌王，宗壽為嘉王，宗翰為集王；

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, adoptive sons were enfeoffed—Zongyu as Prince of Tong, Zongfan as Prince of Kui, Zong Jinsui as Prince of Chang, Zongshou as Prince of Jia, and Zonghan as Prince of Ji;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he enfeoffed his adoptive sons: Zongyu as Prince of Tong, Zongfan as Prince of Kui, Zong Jinsui as Prince of Chang, Zongshou as Prince of Jia, and Zonghan as Prince of Ji;

sentences.zh: 立其子宗仁為普王，宗輅為雅王，宗紀為褒王，宗智為榮王，宗澤為興王，宗鼎為彭王，宗傑為信王，宗衍為鄭王。

translations.literal: His own sons were enfeoffed—Zongren as Prince of Pu, Zonglu as Prince of Ya, Zongji as Prince of Bao, Zongzhi as Prince of Rong, Zongze as Prince of Xing, Zongding as Prince of Peng, Zongjie as Prince of Xin, and Zongyan as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His sons received titles as well: Zongren as Prince of Pu, Zonglu as Prince of Ya, Zongji as Prince of Bao, Zongzhi as Prince of Rong, Zongze as Prince of Xing, Zongding as Prince of Peng, Zongjie as Prince of Xin, and Zongyan as Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 初，唐末宦官典兵者多養軍中壯士為子以自強，由是諸將亦效之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, at the end of Tang many eunuchs who commanded armies adopted stalwart soldiers as sons to strengthen themselves; hence generals also imitated this practice.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tang, eunuch commanders often adopted bold soldiers as sons to bolster their power, and generals soon followed suit.

sentences.zh: 而蜀主尤多，惟宗懿等九人及宗特、宗平真其子；

translations.literal: The Shu ruler had especially many; only Zongyi and the other eight, together with Zongte and Zongping, were truly his sons;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler had more than most; only Zongyi and eight others, along with Zongte and Zongping, were truly his sons;

sentences.zh: 宗裕、宗金歲、宗壽皆其族人；

translations.literal: Zongyu, Zong Jinsui, and Zongshou were all his clansmen;
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu, Zong Jinsui, and Zongshou were all kinsmen;

sentences.zh: 宗翰姓孟，蜀主之姊子；

translations.literal: Zonghan bore the surname Meng; he was the son of the Shu ruler's elder sister;
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan, surname Meng, was the Shu ruler's sister's son;

sentences.zh: 宗范姓張，其母周氏為蜀主妾；

translations.literal: Zongfan bore the surname Zhang; his mother Lady Zhou was a Shu concubine;
translations.idiomatic: Zongfan, surname Zhang, was the son of the concubine Lady Zhou;

sentences.zh: 自餘假子百二十人皆功臣，雖冒姓連名而不禁婚姻。

translations.literal: The remaining one hundred and twenty adoptive sons were all meritorious officials; although they falsely shared surnames and linked names, marriage was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The other hundred twenty adoptive sons were all distinguished men; though they took his surname and bore the "Zong" generation name, marriage among them was not barred.

sentences.zh: 上疾小愈，辛亥，校獵於伊、洛之間。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness had slightly improved; on the day xinhai he conducted a hunting expedition between the Yi and Luo Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: After a slight recovery the emperor went hunting between the Yi and Luo on xinhai.

sentences.zh: 上疑趙王鎔貳於晉，且欲因鄴王紹威卒除移鎮、定。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected that Prince of Zhao Wang Rong was disloyal toward Jin, and also wished to use the death of Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei as an occasion to remove and replace the governors of Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Wang Rong of tilting toward Jin and also hoped to use Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei's death to reshuffle power in Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 會燕王守光發兵屯淶水，欲侵定州，上遣供奉官杜廷隱、丁延徽臨魏博兵三千分屯深、冀，聲言恐燕兵南寇，助趙守禦。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yan Shouguang mobilized troops and encamped at Lishui, intending to invade Ding Prefecture, the emperor sent palace attendants Du Tingyin and Ding Yanhui to take command of three thousand Weibo troops and garrison them separately at Shen and Ji, publicly declaring fear that Yan forces would raid south and claiming to help Zhao defend.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang massed troops at Lishui to threaten Dingzhou, the emperor sent palace attendants Du Tingyin and Ding Yanhui with three thousand Weibo troops to occupy Shen and Ji, claiming they were helping Zhao repel a southern raid by Yan.

sentences.zh: 又雲分兵就食。

translations.literal: They also said they were distributing troops to forage for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: They added that the troops were merely being spread out to live off local supplies.

sentences.zh: 趙將石公立戍深州，白趙王鎔，請拒之。

translations.literal: Zhao general Shi Gongli garrisoned Shen Prefecture and reported to Prince of Zhao Wang Rong, requesting that they be resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao general Shi Gongli, stationed at Shenzhou, warned Wang Rong and asked to turn the Liang troops away.

sentences.zh: 鎔遽命開門，移公立於外以避之。

translations.literal: Rong immediately ordered the gates opened and moved Gongli outside to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Rong at once ordered the gates opened and posted Gongli outside the city to make way.

sentences.zh: 公立出門指城而泣曰：「朱氏滅唐社稷，三尺童子知其為人。

translations.literal: Gongli went out the gate, pointed at the city, and wept, saying, "The Zhu clan destroyed the Tang state; even a three-foot child knows what sort of men they are.
translations.idiomatic: Gongli walked out, pointed back at the city, and wept: "The Zhu clan ruined the Tang—every child knows their kind.

sentences.zh: 而我王猶恃姻好，以長者期之，此所謂開門揖盜者也。

translations.literal: Yet our prince still relies on ties of marriage and expects civilized conduct from them—this is what is called opening the door to invite the thief in.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our prince still trusts the bond of marriage and treats them like gentlemen—this is opening the door to robbers.

sentences.zh: 惜乎，此城之人今為虜矣！

translations.literal: Alas—the people of this city will now become captives!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the people of this city are lost!

sentences.zh: 梁人有亡奔真定，以其謀告鎔者，鎔大懼，又不敢先自絕；

translations.literal: A Liang man fled to Zhending and revealed their plot to Rong; Rong was greatly alarmed but did not dare break off relations first;
translations.idiomatic: A Liang deserter reached Zhending and disclosed the plot; Rong was terrified but did not dare cut ties first;

sentences.zh: 但遣使詣洛陽，訴稱「燕兵已還，與定州講和如故，深、冀民見魏博兵入，奔走驚駭，乞召兵還。

translations.literal: he only sent envoys to Luoyang pleading that "Yan troops have already withdrawn; we have made peace with Ding Prefecture as before; the people of Shen and Ji, seeing Weibo troops enter, fled in panic; we beg that the troops be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: he sent only a plea to Luoyang: "Yan has withdrawn and we are at peace with Dingzhou as before; the people of Shen and Ji panic at the sight of Weibo troops—we ask that they be recalled.

sentences.zh: 」上遣使詣真定慰諭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent envoys to Zhending to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent messengers to Zhending to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廷隱等閉門盡殺趙戍兵，乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Before long Tingyin and the others closed the gates, killed all Zhao garrison troops, seized the walls, and held them in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Du Tingyin's men shut the gates, slaughtered the Zhao garrison, and seized the walls.

sentences.zh: 鎔始命石公立攻之，不克，乃遣使求援於燕、晉。

translations.literal: Rong then ordered Shi Gongli to attack them but could not prevail; he then sent envoys to seek aid from Yan and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong ordered Shi Gongli to retake the city but failed, then appealed to Yan and Jin for help.

sentences.zh: 鎔使者至晉陽，義武節度使王處直使者亦至，欲共推晉王為盟主，合兵攻梁。

translations.literal: When Rong's envoys reached Jinyang, envoys from Yiwu military governor Wang Chuzhi also arrived, wishing jointly to urge the Prince of Jin as alliance leader and unite forces to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's envoys reached Jinyang just as Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu sent his own; both wanted to make the Prince of Jin alliance leader and join forces against Liang.

sentences.zh: 晉王會將佐謀之，皆曰：「鎔久臣朱溫，歲輸重賂，結以婚姻，其交深矣，此必詐也，宜徐觀之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin assembled his officers to deliberate; all said, "Rong has long served Zhu Wen, paying heavy bribes each year and bound by marriage—their ties are deep; this must be a ruse; we should observe slowly.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin consulted his commanders, who all said: "Rong has served Zhu Wen for years, paid him lavish tribute, and married into his house—this must be a trick; watch and wait.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「彼亦擇利害而為之耳。

translations.literal: " The prince said, "He too is simply choosing according to advantage and disadvantage.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince replied, "He is only weighing his interests.

sentences.zh: 王氏在唐世猶或臣或叛，況肯終為朱氏之臣乎？

translations.literal: The Wang clan in the Tang era sometimes submitted and sometimes rebelled—how much less would they willingly remain subjects of the Zhu forever!
translations.idiomatic: The Wangs submitted and rebelled throughout the Tang—why would they stay Zhu subjects forever?

sentences.zh: 彼朱溫之女何如壽安公主！

translations.literal: How does Zhu Wen's daughter compare with Princess Shou'an!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen's daughter is no Princess Shou'an!

sentences.zh: 今救死不贍，何顧婚姻！

translations.literal: Now when saving one's life is impossible, what room is there to consider marriage!
translations.idiomatic: When life is at stake, who cares about a marriage tie!

sentences.zh: 我若疑而不救，正墮朱氏計中。

translations.literal: If we suspect and do not rescue him, we will exactly fall into the Zhu clan's scheme.
translations.idiomatic: If we hesitate and refuse to help, we play straight into Zhu's hands.

sentences.zh: 宜趣發兵赴之，晉、趙葉力，破梁必矣。

translations.literal: We should hurry to dispatch troops to his aid; with Jin and Zhao joining strength, breaking Liang is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Send troops at once; with Jin and Zhao combined, Liang will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 」乃發兵，遣周德威將之，出井陘，屯趙州。

translations.literal: " Accordingly troops were dispatched; Zhou Dewei was sent to command them; they went out through Jingxing Pass and encamped at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He mobilized an army under Zhou Dewei, marched through Jingxing Pass, and camped at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鎔使者至幽州，燕王守光方獵，幕僚孫鶴馳詣野謂守光曰：「趙人來乞師，此天欲成王之功業也。

translations.literal: Rong's envoys reached Youzhou; Prince of Yan Shouguang was just hunting; staff officer Sun He raced to the field and said to Shouguang, "The Zhao people have come to beg for troops—Heaven wishes to complete the king's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's envoys reached Youzhou while Liu Shouguang was hunting; staff officer Sun He rode out to warn him: "Zhao is asking for troops—Heaven is handing you your chance.

sentences.zh: 」守光曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " Shouguang said, "For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: " Shouguang asked, "How so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「比常患其與朱溫膠固。

translations.literal: " He replied, "We have long worried that they were firmly glued to Zhu Wen.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun He said, "We have long feared their tight bond with Zhu Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫之志非盡吞河朔不已，今彼自為仇敵，王若與之並力破梁，則鎮、定皆斂衣任而朝燕矣。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen's ambition is to swallow all of Hebei and not stop; now they have made themselves enemies; if the king joins forces with them to break Liang, then Zhen and Ding will both straighten their robes and present themselves at court before Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen will not rest until he devours Hebei; now Zhao has turned enemy against him—join them, break Liang, and Zhen and Ding will bow to Yan.

sentences.zh: 王不早出師，但恐晉人先我矣。

translations.literal: If the king does not march out early, I fear only that the Jin people will get ahead of us.
translations.idiomatic: If you delay, Jin will beat us to it.

sentences.zh: 」守光曰：「王鎔數負約，今使之與梁自相弊，吾可以坐承其利，又何救焉！

translations.literal: " Shouguang said, "Wang Rong has repeatedly broken faith; let him and Liang wear each other down—I can sit and reap the profit; why rescue him!
translations.idiomatic: " Shouguang said, "Wang Rong breaks his word at every turn—let him and Liang bleed each other while I sit back and profit. Why should I save him?

sentences.zh: 」趙使者交錯於路，守光竟不為出兵。

translations.literal: " Zhao envoys crisscrossed on the road, but Shouguang in the end would not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Envoys kept arriving from Zhao, but Shouguang never sent an army.

sentences.zh: 自是鎮、定復稱唐天祐年號，復以武順為成德軍。

translations.literal: From this Zhen and Ding again used the Tang Tianyou reign era and again renamed Wushun as Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Ding thereafter restored the Tang Tianyou reign title and renamed the circuit Wushun back to Chengde.

sentences.zh: 司天言：「來月太陰虧，不利宿兵於外。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported, "Next month the moon will be eclipsed—unfavorable to keep troops encamped abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The astronomy office warned: "Next month's lunar eclipse bodes ill for armies camped in the field.

sentences.zh: 」上召王景仁等還洛陽。

translations.literal: " The emperor recalled Wang Jingren and the others to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor recalled Wang Jingren to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己未，上聞趙與晉合，晉兵已屯趙州，乃命王景仁等將兵擊之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiwei, the emperor heard that Zhao had joined with Jin and Jin troops had already encamped at Zhao Prefecture; he then ordered Wang Jingren and the others to lead troops and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiwei, learning that Zhao and Jin had allied and Jin was camped at Zhao Prefecture, he ordered Wang Jingren to attack.

sentences.zh: 庚申，景仁等自河陽渡河，會羅周翰兵，合四萬，軍於邢、洺。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Jingren and the others crossed the Yellow River from Heyang, joined Luo Zhouhan's troops, totaled forty thousand, and encamped at Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Wang Jingren crossed from Heyang, joined Luo Zhouhan, and massed forty thousand men at Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 虔州刺史盧光稠疾病，欲以位授譚全播，全播不受。

translations.literal: Qian Prefecture prefect Lu Guangchou was ill and wished to give his post to Tan Quanbo; Quanbo would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou prefect Lu Guangchou fell ill and tried to hand his post to Tan Quanbo, who refused.

sentences.zh: 光稠卒，其子韶州刺史延昌來奔喪，全播立而事之。

translations.literal: Guangchou died; his son Yanchang, prefect of Shao Prefecture, came to mourn; Quanbo installed him and served him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangchou died his son Yanchang, prefect of Shaozhou, came for the funeral; Quanbo placed him in authority and served him.

sentences.zh: 吳遣使拜延昌虔州刺史，延昌受之，亦因楚王殷通密表於梁，曰：「我受淮南官，以緩其謀耳，必為朝廷經略江西。

translations.literal: Wu sent envoys to appoint Yanchang prefect of Qian Prefecture; Yanchang accepted; he also secretly memorialized Liang through Prince of Chu Yin Tong, saying, "I accepted office from Huainan only to stall their plans; I will surely carry out the court's strategy for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu recognized Yanchang as Qianzhou prefect and he accepted, but he secretly wrote Liang through Prince of Chu Yin Tong: "I took Huainan's commission only to buy time—I mean to secure Jiangxi for the throne.

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，以延昌為鎮南留後。

translations.literal: " On the day bingyin, Yanchang was made acting governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: " On bingyin Yanchang was appointed acting Zhennan governor.

sentences.zh: 延昌表其將廖爽為韶州刺史，爽，贛人也。

translations.literal: Yanchang memorialized recommending his general Liao Shuang as prefect of Shao Prefecture; Shuang was a native of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang recommended his general Liao Shuang, a man of Gan, for Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 吳淮南節度判官嚴可求請置制置使於新淦縣，遣兵戍之，以圖虔州。

translations.literal: Wu Huainan circuit administrative aide Yan Keqiu requested that a commissioner for special operations be established at Xingan County and troops garrisoned there to target Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu aide Yan Keqiu of Huainan proposed a special commissioner at Xingan County with a garrison aimed at Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 每更代，輒潛益其兵，虔人不之覺也。

translations.literal: With each rotation of personnel, they secretly increased the troops; the people of Qian Prefecture did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Each rotation of troops brought a quiet increase in strength that the people of Qianzhou never noticed.

sentences.zh: 庚午，蜀主以御史中丞周庠、戶部侍郎判度支庾傳素並為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the Shu ruler made Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Kuang and Ministry of Revenue Vice Minister and fiscal commissioner Yu Chuansu both Vice Directors of the Chancellery and co-equal chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the Shu ruler named Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Kuang and fiscal commissioner Yu Chuansu co-equal chief ministers and vice directors of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 太常卿李燕等刊定《梁律令格式》，癸酉，行之。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices director Li Yan and others revised the Liang Statutes, Orders, Models, and Formats; on the day guiyou they were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and others finalized the Liang law code; it took effect on guiyou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，王景仁等進軍柏鄉。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Wang Jingren and the others advanced the army to Baixiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wang Jingren marched on Baixiang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，蜀大赦，改明年元曰永平。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Shu declared a general amnesty and changed next year's reign title to Everlasting Peace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and named the coming year Everlasting Peace.

sentences.zh: 趙王鎔復告急於晉，晉王以蕃漢副總管李存審守晉陽，自將兵自讚皇東下，王處直遣將將兵五千以從。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Wang Rong again reported an emergency to Jin; the Prince of Jin left Han-Chinese deputy commander Li Cunshen to guard Jinyang and personally led troops east from Zanhuang; Wang Chuzhi sent a general with five thousand troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong again appealed urgently to Jin; the Prince of Jin left Li Cunshen at Jinyang and led the main army east from Zanhuang, with five thousand men from Wang Chuzhi in support.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，晉王至趙州，與周德威合，獲梁芻蕘者二百人，問之曰：「初發洛陽，梁主有何號令？

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the Prince of Jin reached Zhao Prefecture, joined Zhou Dewei, and captured two hundred Liang foragers; he questioned them, saying, "When you first set out from Luoyang, what orders did the Liang ruler give?
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Prince of Jin reached Zhao Prefecture, linked up with Zhou Dewei, and seized two hundred Liang foragers. He asked them: "When you left Luoyang, what were the Liang ruler's orders?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「梁主戒上將云：『鎮州反覆，終為子孫之患。

translations.literal: " They replied, "The Liang ruler warned his chief generals, saying, 'Zhen Prefecture is fickle—in the end it will be a disaster for our descendants.
translations.idiomatic: " They said: "The Liang ruler warned his commanders: 'Zhenzhou is treacherous—it will haunt your heirs.

sentences.zh: 今悉以精兵付汝，鎮州雖以鐵為城，必為我取之。

translations.literal: Now I entrust all elite troops to you; though Zhen Prefecture were walled in iron, you must take it for me.
translations.idiomatic: I give you every crack soldier; even if Zhenzhou were iron-walled, you must take it for me.

sentences.zh: 』」晉王命送於趙。

translations.literal: '" The Prince of Jin ordered them sent to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: '" The prince sent them on to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 壬午，晉王進軍，距柏鄉三十里，遣周德威等以胡騎迫梁營挑戰，梁兵不出。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the Prince of Jin advanced; thirty li from Baixiang he sent Zhou Dewei and others with barbarian cavalry to press the Liang camp and provoke battle; Liang troops did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the prince advanced to within thirty li of Baixiang and sent Zhou Dewei with allied cavalry to taunt the Liang camp; the Liang army refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 癸未，復進，距柏鄉五里，營於野河之北，又遣胡騎迫梁營馳射，且詬之。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, he advanced again; five li from Baixiang he encamped north of the Yegou River; he again sent barbarian cavalry to press the Liang camp with mounted archery and cursed them besides.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he pushed to within five li of Baixiang and camped north of the Yegou River, again sending cavalry to skirmish and hurl insults at the Liang lines.

sentences.zh: 梁將韓勍等將步騎三萬，分三道追之，鎧冑皆被繒綺，鏤金銀，光彩炫耀，晉人望之奪氣。

translations.literal: Liang generals Han Qing and others led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, pursuing in three columns; their armor was all draped in silk brocade inlaid with gold and silver, dazzling in splendor; the Jin men lost heart at the sight.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Han Qing led thirty thousand horse and foot in three columns, armor draped in brocade set with gold and silver so dazzling the Jin troops lost heart just looking.

sentences.zh: 周德威謂李存璋曰：「梁人志不在戰，徒欲曜兵耳。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei said to Li Cunzhang, "The Liang men's intent is not to fight; they merely wish to display their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei told Li Cunzhang: "The Liang aren't here to fight—they only want to show off.

sentences.zh: 不挫其銳，則吾軍不振。

translations.literal: If we do not blunt their edge, our army will not be roused.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we blunt their swagger, our men won't recover their spirit.

sentences.zh: 」乃徇於軍曰：「彼皆汴州天武軍，屠酤人庸販之徒耳，衣鎧雖鮮，十不能當汝一。

translations.literal: 」He then proclaimed throughout the army, saying, "Those men are all from the Tianwu Army of Bian Prefecture—nothing but butchers, wine-sellers, hired laborers, and peddlers; though their armor is bright, ten of them cannot match one of you.
translations.idiomatic: 」He then rallied the troops: "They're all Tianwu men from Bian—butchers, tavern keepers, day-laborers, and hawkers. Their armor may glitter, but ten of them won't equal one of you.

sentences.zh: 擒獲一夫，足以自富，此乃奇貨，不可失也。

translations.literal: Capture a single man and you will be rich enough on your own—this is a rare prize; do not let it slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Take one prisoner and you're set for life. This is treasure on legs—don't let it get away.

sentences.zh: 」德威自帥精騎千餘擊其兩端，左馳右突，出入數四，俘獲百餘人，且戰且卻，距野河而止。

translations.literal: 」Dewei himself led more than a thousand elite horsemen to strike both flanks, charging left and dashing right, entering and withdrawing four times; he captured more than a hundred men, fighting as he withdrew, and stopped when he reached the Wild River.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dewei personally led a thousand crack cavalry against both ends of their line, wheeling left and right, striking in and pulling back four times. He took over a hundred prisoners, fighting all the way back until he halted at the Wild River.

sentences.zh: 梁兵亦退。

translations.literal: The Liang troops also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army pulled back as well.

sentences.zh: 德威言於晉王曰：「賊勢甚盛，宜按兵以待其衰。

translations.literal: Dewei said to the Prince of Jin, "The enemy's momentum is very strong; we should hold our troops in check and wait for it to wane.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei told the Prince of Jin, "The enemy is at full strength—we should hold back and let that strength spend itself.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「吾孤軍遠來，救人之急，三鎮烏合，利於速戰，公乃欲按兵持重，何也？

translations.literal: 」The prince said, "I have come far with an isolated force to rescue men in urgent need; the three garrisons have joined in haste—the advantage lies in a swift battle. Yet you wish to hold the army back and act with ponderous caution—why?
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince replied, "I marched here from afar with a single army to relieve a desperate ally. Three commands have thrown themselves together—we win by striking fast. You want to sit tight and play it safe. Why?

sentences.zh: 」德威曰：「鎮、定之兵，長於守城，短於野戰。

translations.literal: 」Dewei said, "The troops of Zhen and Ding excel at holding cities but are weak in field combat.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dewei said, "Zhen and Ding men are good behind walls and poor in the open field.

sentences.zh: 且吾所恃者騎兵，利於平原廣野，可以馳突。

translations.literal: Moreover, what we rely on is cavalry, which favors broad plains and open country where it can charge and raid.
translations.idiomatic: We depend on cavalry, which needs open ground to run and strike.

sentences.zh: 今壓賊壘門，騎無所展其足。

translations.literal: Now we press against the enemy's ramparts; the cavalry have nowhere to stretch their legs.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed up against their fortifications, our horsemen have no room to maneuver.

sentences.zh: 且眾寡不敵，使彼知吾虛實，則事危矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, we are outnumbered; if they learn our true strength and weakness, the situation will become perilous.
translations.idiomatic: We are too few. If they learn our real numbers, we're in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 」王不悅，退臥帳中，諸將莫敢言。

translations.literal: 」The prince was displeased; he withdrew and lay down in his tent, and none of the generals dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince took offense, retired to his tent, and lay down. None of the generals dared say another word.

sentences.zh: 德威往見張承業曰：「大王驟勝而輕敵，不量力而務速戰。

translations.literal: Dewei went to see Zhang Chengye and said, "Our lord, fresh from sudden victory, underestimates the enemy and, without measuring his strength, insists on a swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei sought out Zhang Chengye. "Fresh off a quick win, His Highness is treating the enemy lightly—ignoring the odds and pushing for immediate battle.

sentences.zh: 今去賊咫尺，所限者一水耳。

translations.literal: At present we are a hand's breadth from the enemy; only a river stands between us.
translations.idiomatic: We're a stone's throw from the enemy—only a river away.

sentences.zh: 彼若造橋以薄我，我眾立盡矣。

translations.literal: If they build bridges to press upon us, our forces will be wiped out in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: If they throw up bridges and close in, our army will be destroyed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 不若退軍高邑，誘賊離營，彼出則歸，彼歸則出，別以輕騎掠其饋餉，不過逾月，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Better to withdraw the army to Gaoyi, lure the enemy away from camp—when they come out we withdraw, when they withdraw we come out—and separately send light cavalry to raid their provisions; within no more than a month, defeating them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Better to fall back on Gaoyi and bait them out of camp—hit and fade, fade and hit—while light cavalry strips their supply lines. Give it a month and they'll break.

sentences.zh: 」承業入褰帳撫王曰：「此豈王安寢時耶！

translations.literal: 」Chengye entered, drew aside the tent curtain, and soothed the prince, saying, "Is this a time for Your Highness to sleep in peace!
translations.idiomatic: 」Chengye parted the tent flap and roused the prince. "This is no hour for sleeping!

sentences.zh: 周德威老將知兵，其言不可忽也。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei is an old general who knows warfare; his words must not be disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei is a veteran who knows war. You cannot ignore him.

sentences.zh: 」王蹶然興曰：「予方思之。

translations.literal: 」The prince suddenly sat up and said, "I was just thinking about that.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince bolted upright. "I was just turning it over in my mind.

sentences.zh: 」時梁兵閉壘不出，有降者，詰之，曰：「景仁方多造浮橋。

translations.literal: 」At that time the Liang troops closed their fortifications and would not come out; there were deserters, and when questioned they said, "Jingren is building many pontoon bridges.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Liang army had shut themselves in. Interrogating a deserter, they learned, "Jingren is mass-producing pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 」王謂德威曰：「果如公言。

translations.literal: 」The prince said to Dewei, "It has turned out exactly as you said.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince told Dewei, "Just as you predicted.

sentences.zh: 」是日，拔營，退保高邑。

translations.literal: 」That day they struck camp and withdrew to hold Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: 」That same day they broke camp and fell back to Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 辰州蠻酋宋鄴，漵州蠻酋潘金盛，恃其所居深險，數擾楚邊。

translations.literal: Song Ye, chieftain of the Chenzhou barbarians, and Pan Jinsheng, chieftain of the Xuzhou barbarians, relied on the deep perilous terrain where they dwelt and repeatedly harassed the Chu border.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ye, a Chenzhou tribal chief, and Pan Jinsheng, a Xuzhou tribal chief, trusted their rugged mountain strongholds and raided the Chu frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 至是，鄴寇湘鄉，金盛寇武岡，楚王殷遣昭州刺史呂師周將衡山兵五千討之。

translations.literal: At this time Ye raided Xiangxiang and Jinsheng raided Wugang; King Yin of Chu sent Zhaozhou prefect Lü Shizhou at the head of five thousand Hengshan troops to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ye struck Xiangxiang and Jinsheng struck Wugang. King Ma Yin of Chu sent Lü Shizhou, prefect of Zhaozhou, with five thousand Hengshan soldiers against them.

sentences.zh: 寧遠節度使龐巨昭、高州防禦使劉昌魯，皆唐官也。

translations.literal: Pang Juzhao, military governor of Ningyuan, and Liu Changlu, defense commissioner of Gaozhou, were both Tang officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ningyuan military governor Pang Juzhao and Gaozhou defense commissioner Liu Changlu had both served as Tang officials.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之寇嶺南也，巨昭為容管觀察使，昌魯為高州刺史，帥群蠻據險以拒之，巢眾不敢入境。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao raided Lingnan, Juzhao was Rongguan observation commissioner and Changlu was prefect of Gaozhou; they led the tribal groups to hold the passes and resist him, and Chao's host did not dare enter the territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao swept through Lingnan, Juzhao was Rongguan observation commissioner and Changlu was Gaozhou prefect. They rallied the tribes to hold the passes; Chao's army never crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 唐嘉其功，置寧遠軍於容州，以巨昭為節度使，以昌魯為高州防禦使。

translations.literal: Tang rewarded their merit by establishing the Ningyuan army at Rong Prefecture, making Juzhao military governor and Changlu defense commissioner of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang honored their service by creating the Ningyuan command at Rongzhou, appointing Juzhao its governor and Changlu defense commissioner of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 及劉隱據嶺南，二州不從；

translations.literal: When Liu Yin seized Lingnan, the two prefectures did not submit;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yin took control of Lingnan, neither prefecture bowed to him;

sentences.zh: 隱遣弟巖攻高州，昌魯大破之，又攻容州，亦不克。

translations.literal: Yin sent his younger brother Yan to attack Gaozhou; Changlu routed him severely, and when he attacked Rong Prefecture as well, he likewise could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent his brother Yan against Gaozhou; Changlu crushed him. Yan then turned on Rongzhou and failed again.

sentences.zh: 昌魯自度終非隱敵，是歲，致書請自歸於楚。

translations.literal: Changlu reckoned that in the end he could not match Yin as an enemy; that year he sent a letter asking to submit himself to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu decided he could never best Yin. That year he wrote offering to come over to Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷大喜，遣橫州刺史姚彥章將兵迎之。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu was greatly pleased and sent Hengzhou prefect Yao Yanzhang with troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: King Ma Yin was delighted and dispatched Yao Yanzhang, prefect of Hengzhou, with an escort.

sentences.zh: 彥章至容州，裨將莫彥昭說巨昭曰：「湖南兵遠來疲乏，宜撤儲偫，棄城，潛於山谷以待之。

translations.literal: When Yanzhang reached Rong Prefecture, deputy general Mo Yanzhao urged Juzhao, saying, "The Hunan troops have come from afar and are weary; we should remove stored supplies, abandon the city, and lie hidden in the valleys to wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: At Rongzhou, deputy commander Mo Yanzhao advised Juzhao: "The Hunan army is exhausted from the long march. Empty the granaries, abandon the city, and hide in the hills—

sentences.zh: 彼必入城，我以全軍掩之，彼外無繼援，可擒也。

translations.literal: They are sure to enter the city; we then fall upon them with our full force—they will have no reinforcements from outside, and we can capture them.
translations.idiomatic: They'll walk straight in. Then we hit them with everything we've got. Cut off from relief, they're ours.

sentences.zh: 」巨昭曰：「馬氏方興，今雖勝之，後將何如！

translations.literal: 」Juzhao said, "The Ma house is on the rise; even if we defeat them now, what will become of us afterward!
translations.idiomatic: 」Juzhao said, "The Mas are ascendant. Beat them today—and then what?

sentences.zh: 不若具牛酒迎之。

translations.literal: Better to prepare oxen and wine to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to greet them with cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 」彥昭不從，巨昭殺之，舉州迎降。

translations.literal: 」Yanzhao would not agree; Juzhao killed him and surrendered the whole prefecture in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yanzhao refused. Juzhao had him killed and surrendered the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥章進至高州，以兵援送巨昭、昌魯之族及士卒千餘人歸長沙。

translations.literal: Yanzhang advanced to Gaozhou and escorted the clans of Juzhao and Changlu plus more than a thousand soldiers back to Changsha under armed guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang pushed on to Gaozhou and convoyed the families of Juzhao and Changlu, along with a thousand-odd troops, back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷以彥章知容州事，以昌魯為永順節度副使。

translations.literal: King Yin put Yanzhang in charge of Rong Prefecture affairs and made Changlu vice military governor of Yongshun.
translations.idiomatic: King Yin put Yanzhang in charge of Rongzhou and made Changlu vice governor of Yongshun.

sentences.zh: 昌魯，鄴人也。

translations.literal: Changlu was a native of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Changlu came from Ye.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Spring, the first month; on the day bingxu, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month—bingxu—a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉比不儲芻，梁兵刈芻自給，晉人日以遊軍抄之，梁兵不出。

translations.literal: Baixiang had never stored fodder; the Liang troops cut grass to supply themselves, and the Jin men daily sent raiding parties to intercept it; the Liang troops did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Baixiang had no fodder reserves. Liang soldiers scoured the fields for forage while Jin patrols picked off the foragers daily. The Liang army stayed inside.

sentences.zh: 周德威使胡騎環營馳射而詬之，梁兵疑有伏，愈不敢出，坐刀屋茅坐席以飼馬，馬多死。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei sent allied cavalry to circle the camp, shooting as they galloped and hurling insults; the Liang troops suspected an ambush and grew ever less willing to emerge, using blade-roof shelters and straw mat seats to feed the horses; many horses died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei sent allied cavalry to ride rings around the camp, loosing arrows and taunts. The Liang army, fearing ambush, dug in further. They fed their horses under makeshift blade-roof shelters on straw matting; horses died in droves.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，周德威與別將史建瑭、李嗣源將精騎三千壓梁壘門而詬之，王景仁、韓勍怒，悉眾而出。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Zhou Dewei with separate commanders Shi Jiantan and Li Siyuan led three thousand elite horsemen to press the Liang ramparts and hurl insults; Wang Jingren and Han Qing, enraged, led out their entire force.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Zhou Dewei with Shi Jiantan and Li Siyuan drove three thousand crack cavalry to the Liang gates, jeering. Wang Jingren and Han Qing, furious, marched out with their full strength.

sentences.zh: 德威等轉戰而北至高邑南；

translations.literal: Dewei and the others fought in withdrawal northward to south of Gaoyi;
translations.idiomatic: Dewei's force fought a fighting retreat north to the south of Gaoyi;

sentences.zh: 李存璋以步兵陳於野河之上，梁軍橫亙數里，競前奪橋，鎮、定步兵御之，勢不能支。

translations.literal: Li Cunzhang drew up infantry above the Wild River; the Liang army stretched across several li, racing forward to seize the bridge; the Zhen and Ding infantry resisted them but could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunzhang formed infantry along the Wild River. The Liang line stretched for miles, surging for the bridge. Zhen and Ding foot soldiers held but were buckling.

sentences.zh: 晉王謂匡衛都指揮使李建及曰：「賊過橋則不可複製矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin said to Kuangwei director-general Li Jianji, "If the bandits cross the bridge, they cannot be stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin told Li Jianji, commander of the Kuangwei Guard, "Once they cross that bridge, we lose them forever.

sentences.zh: 」建及選卒二百，援槍大噪，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: 」Jianji selected two hundred soldiers, seized spears, raised a great clamor, and fought fiercely to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jianji picked two hundred men, spears in hand, and with a roaring charge fought them back.

sentences.zh: 建及，許州人，姓王，李罕之之假子也。

translations.literal: Jianji was a native of Xuzhou; his surname was Wang; he was the adopted son of Li Hanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji, born in Xuzhou, bore the surname Wang and was the adopted son of Li Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 晉王登高丘以望曰：「梁兵爭進而囂，我兵整而靜，我必勝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin climbed a high hill to look and said, "The Liang troops press forward in disorder and clamor; our troops are formed and quiet—we are sure to win.
translations.idiomatic: From a hilltop the Prince of Jin watched and said, "The Liang army pushes forward in chaos and noise. Ours holds steady and silent. We will win.

sentences.zh: 」戰自巳至午，勝負未決。

translations.literal: 」The battle ran from the si hour to the wu hour; victory and defeat were still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: 」Fighting lasted from mid-morning until noon with no clear victor.

sentences.zh: 晉王謂周德威曰：「兩軍已合，勢不可離，我之興亡，在此一舉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin said to Zhou Dewei, "The two armies have already joined; momentum cannot be broken—our rise or fall hangs on this one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The prince told Zhou Dewei, "The armies are locked together. We can't pull apart now—everything rides on this charge.

sentences.zh: 我為公先登，公可繼之。

translations.literal: I will take the lead for you; you may follow.
translations.idiomatic: I'll go first—you follow.

sentences.zh: 」德威叩馬而諫曰：「觀梁兵之勢，可以勞逸制之，未易以力勝也。

translations.literal: 」Dewei grasped the prince's horse and remonstrated, saying, "Judging by the Liang troops' posture, they can be mastered through weariness against rest; it is not easy to win by main force.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dewei seized the prince's bridle. "Look at their line—we can beat them with fatigue, not a frontal rush.

sentences.zh: 彼去營三十餘里，雖挾糗糧，亦不暇食，日昳之後，飢渴內迫，矢刃外交，士卒勞倦，必有退志。

translations.literal: They are more than thirty li from camp; though they carry dry rations, they have no time to eat; after the sun passes the meridian, hunger and thirst will press from within while arrows and blades press from without; the soldiers, weary from labor, are bound to want to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: They're thirty li from camp. They brought rations but haven't had time to eat. After midday, hunger and thirst will gnaw at them while blades press from every side. Their men are exhausted—they'll want out.

sentences.zh: 當是時，我以精騎乘之，必大捷。

translations.literal: At that moment, if we strike with elite cavalry, a great victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: That's when we hit them with our best cavalry—a crushing win.

sentences.zh: 於今未可也。

translations.literal: For the present it is not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet.

sentences.zh: 」王乃止。

translations.literal: 」The prince then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The prince held back.

sentences.zh: 時魏、滑之兵陳於東、宋、汴之兵陳於西。

translations.literal: At the time the Wei and Hua troops were arrayed on the east and the Song and Bian troops on the west.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Hua units held the east; Song and Bian units the west.

sentences.zh: 至晡，梁軍未食，士無鬥志，景仁等引兵稍卻，周德威疾呼曰：「梁兵走矣！

translations.literal: By the hour of shen, the Liang army had not eaten; the soldiers had no will to fight; Jingren and the others slowly withdrew their troops; Zhou Dewei shouted urgently, "The Liang troops are fleeing!
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the Liang army had eaten nothing. Morale collapsed. Jingren began to pull back. Zhou Dewei shouted, "They're running!

sentences.zh: 」晉兵大噪爭進，魏、滑兵先退，李嗣源帥眾噪於西陳之前曰：「東陳已走，爾何久留！

translations.literal: 」The Jin troops raised a great clamor and pressed forward; the Wei and Hua troops retreated first; Li Siyuan led his force shouting before the western formation, "The eastern formation has already fled—why do you linger so long!
translations.idiomatic: 」Jin troops roared forward. Wei and Hua broke first. Li Siyuan rode before the western line shouting, "The east wing is gone—what are you still doing here!

sentences.zh: 」梁兵互相驚怖，遂大潰。

translations.literal: 」The Liang troops, mutually alarmed and terrified, then broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: 」Panic spread through the Liang ranks and they collapsed.

sentences.zh: 李存璋引步兵乘之，呼曰：「梁人亦吾人也，父兄子弟餉軍者勿殺。

translations.literal: Li Cunzhang led infantry in pursuit and shouted, "The Liang men are also our people—do not kill fathers, elder brothers, younger brothers, and sons who bring provisions to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunzhang drove the infantry after them, crying, "Liang soldiers are our own people—spare the kin who came only to bring supplies!

sentences.zh: 」於是戰士悉解甲投兵而棄之，囂聲動天地。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon the fighting men all stripped armor, cast down weapons, and abandoned them; the clamor shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: 」Soldiers shed armor and dropped weapons by the thousand—the din shook the sky.

sentences.zh: 趙人以深、冀之憾，不顧剽掠，但奮白刃追之，梁之龍驤、神捷精兵殆盡，自野河至柏鄉，殭屍蔽地。

translations.literal: The Zhao men, nursing grievances over Shen and Ji, paid no heed to plunder but only brandished naked blades in pursuit; the Dragon Flying and Divine Swift elite troops of Liang were nearly annihilated; from the Wild River to Baixiang, corpses covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao soldiers, still burning over Shen and Ji, ignored loot and chased with naked steel. Liang's Dragon Flying and Divine Swift elites were virtually wiped out. From the Wild River to Baixiang, the dead carpeted the earth.

sentences.zh: 王景仁、韓勍、李思安以數十騎走。

translations.literal: Wang Jingren, Han Qing, and Li Si'an fled with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingren, Han Qing, and Li Si'an escaped with a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 晉兵夜至柏鄉，梁軍已去，棄糧食、資財、器械不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Jin troops reached Baixiang by night; the Liang army had already gone, abandoning food, wealth, and weapons beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops reached Baixiang by night. The Liang army was gone, leaving food, treasure, and weapons beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 凡斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: In all, twenty thousand heads were severed.
translations.idiomatic: The dead numbered twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源等追奔至邢州，河朔大震。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan and the others pursued the rout to Xing Prefecture; the whole Hebei region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan's pursuit reached Xingzhou. All of Hebei reeled.

sentences.zh: 保義節度使王檀嚴備，然後開城納敗卒，給以資糧，散遣歸本道。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, military governor of Baoyi, made strict preparations and then opened the city to admit defeated soldiers, supplied them with provisions and funds, and dispersed them to return to their home circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi governor Wang Tan stood ready, then opened his gates to the survivors, gave them provisions, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 晉王收兵屯趙州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin gathered his troops and encamped at Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin pulled his army together at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 杜廷隱等聞梁兵敗，棄深、冀而去，悉驅二州丁壯為奴婢，老弱者坑之，城中存者壞垣而已。

translations.literal: When Du Tingyin and the others heard that the Liang army was defeated, they abandoned Shen and Ji and fled, driving all the able-bodied men and women of the two prefectures off as slaves and servants, burying the old and weak alive; of those who remained in the cities, only broken walls were left.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, Du Tingyin and his cohort abandoned Shen and Ji. They marched every able-bodied man and woman off as slaves and buried the old and weak alive. The cities held nothing but broken walls.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，復以楊師厚為北面都招討使，將兵屯河陽，收集散兵，旬餘，得萬人。

translations.literal: On guisi, Yang Shihou was again appointed overall northern campaign commander; he led troops to encamp at Heyang and gathered scattered soldiers; in a little more than ten days he collected ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Yang Shihou was reappointed northern campaign commander. He camped at Heyang, rallied stragglers, and within ten days had ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 己亥，晉王遣周德威、史建瑭將三千騎趣澶、魏，張承業、李存璋以步兵攻邢州，自以大軍繼之，移檄河北州縣，諭以利害。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantan with three thousand horsemen toward Chan and Wei; Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang attacked Xing Prefecture with infantry while he followed with the main army, issuing proclamations to the prefectures and counties of Hebei to explain advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantan with three thousand cavalry toward Chan and Wei. Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang hit Xingzhou with infantry while the main army followed. Proclamations went out across Hebei spelling out the stakes.

sentences.zh: 帝遣別將徐仁溥將兵千人，自西山夜入邢州，助王檀城守。

translations.literal: The emperor sent separate commander Xu Renpu with a thousand troops to enter Xing Prefecture by night from the western mountains to help Wang Tan hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xu Renpu with a thousand men into Xingzhou by night through the western hills to reinforce Wang Tan.

sentences.zh: 己酉，罷王景仁招討使，落平章事。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wang Jingren was removed as campaign commander and stripped of his grand councilor title.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Wang Jingren lost his campaign command and his grand councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 蜀主之女普慈公主嫁岐王從子秦州節度使繼崇，公主遣宦者宋光嗣以絹書遣蜀主，言繼崇驕矜嗜酒，求歸成都，蜀主召公主歸寧。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler's daughter, Princess Puci, had married Jichong, nephew of the Prince of Qi and military governor of Qin Prefecture; the princess sent the eunuch Song Guangsi with a letter written on silk to the Shu ruler, saying Jichong was arrogant, proud, and fond of wine, and asking to return to Chengdu; the Shu ruler summoned the princess home for a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Puci, the Shu ruler's daughter, had married Jichong—the Prince of Qi's nephew and Qinzhou governor. She sent the eunuch Song Guangsi with a silk letter complaining that Jichong was proud and drunken, begging to come home. The Shu ruler summoned her for a visit.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公主至成都，蜀主留之，以宋光嗣為閣門南院使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the princess reached Chengdu; the Shu ruler kept her there and made Song Guangsi commissioner of the Southern Gate Office of the Inner Portal.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the princess arrived in Chengdu. The Shu ruler kept her there and made Song Guangsi commissioner of the inner southern gate.

sentences.zh: 岐王怒，始與蜀絕。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was enraged and broke with Shu for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, furious, cut ties with Shu.

sentences.zh: 光嗣，福州人也。

translations.literal: Guangsi was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 呂師周引兵攀籐緣崖入飛山洞襲潘金盛，擒送武岡，斬之。

translations.literal: Lü Shizhou led troops climbing vines along cliffs to enter Feishan Cave and surprise Pan Jinsheng; he captured him, sent him to Wugang, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shizhou's men scaled cliffs on vines, burst into Feishan Cave, and seized Pan Jinsheng. They took him to Wugang and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 移兵擊宋鄴。

translations.literal: He shifted his troops to attack Song Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his army against Song Ye.

sentences.zh: 二月，己未，晉王至魏州，攻之，不克。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiwei, the Prince of Jin reached Wei Prefecture and attacked it but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiwei, the Prince of Jin besieged Wei Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 上以羅周翰年少，且忌其舊將佐，庚申，以戶部尚書李振為天雄節度副使，命杜廷隱將兵千人衛之，自楊劉濟河，間道夜入魏州，助周翰城守。

translations.literal: Because Luo Zhouhan was young and the emperor also mistrusted his old generals and staff, on gengshen he appointed Li Zhen, minister of revenue, as vice military governor of Tianxiong, ordered Du Tingyin to escort him with a thousand troops, crossed the Yellow River at Yangliu, entered Wei Prefecture by a secret route at night, and helped Zhouhan hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, doubting young Luo Zhouhan and his veteran staff, on gengshen sent Revenue Minister Li Zhen as Tianxiong vice governor. Du Tingyin escorted him with a thousand men across the Yellow River at Yangliu, slipped into Wei Prefecture by night, and helped Zhouhan prepare the defense.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，晉王觀河於黎陽，梁兵萬餘將渡河，聞晉王至，皆棄舟而去。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Prince of Jin observed the river at Liyang; more than ten thousand Liang troops were about to cross the river, but when they heard the Prince of Jin had arrived, they all abandoned their boats and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the Prince of Jin surveyed the river at Liyang. Ten thousand Liang soldiers were about to cross—but at news of his arrival they abandoned their boats and ran.

sentences.zh: 帝召蔡州刺史張慎思至洛陽，久未除代。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Caizhou prefect Zhang Senshi to Luoyang and for a long time did not appoint a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Caizhou prefect Zhang Senshi to Luoyang and left the prefecture without a successor for months.

sentences.zh: 蔡州右廂指揮使劉行琮作亂，縱兵焚掠，將奔淮南；

translations.literal: Caizhou right-wing commander Liu Xingcong revolted, let his troops burn and plunder, and prepared to flee to Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: Caizhou's right-wing commander Liu Xingcong mutinied, letting his men burn and loot as he prepared to flee to Huainan;

sentences.zh: 順化指揮使王存儼誅行琮，撫遏其眾，自領州事，以眾情馳奏。

translations.literal: Shunhua commander Wang Cunyan executed Xingcong, pacified and restrained the multitude, took charge of prefectural affairs himself, and dispatched a fast report on the army's sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Shunhua commander Wang Cunyan killed Xingcong, calmed the troops, took command himself, and sent an urgent report to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時東京留守博王友文不先請，遽發兵討之，兵至鄢陵，帝曰：「存儼方懼，若臨之以兵，則飛去矣。

translations.literal: At the time the Eastern Capital caretaker, Prince Bo Youwen, without prior permission hastily sent troops to suppress him; when the troops reached Yanling, the emperor said, "Cunyan is still frightened; if we press him with troops, he will fly away.
